INTRODUCTION
 
       I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
 Culture, having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this One
 Hundred and Twenty Fifth Report of the Committee on Action Taken by the Government on the
 Recommendations/Observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred and Sixteenth Report
 on Demands for Grants (2007-08) of Ministry of Civil Aviation.
 
2.     The One Hundred and Sixteenth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing
 Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the 14
th May 2007. 
 
 
3.   The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred
 and Sixteenth Report were received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 10
th October, 2007.
 
4.   The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 2nd November, 2007.
 
 
 
 
                                               
 
 
NEW DELHI ;
November 2, 2007
Kartika 11, 1929 (Saka)
SITARAM YECH
 Chairman
           Department-related Parliamentary Standing
 Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture.
 
 
 
 
REPORT
This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on
 the observations/ recommendations as contained in its One-Hundred and Sixteenth Report on Demands
 for Grants (2007-08) of Ministry of Civil Aviation , which was presented to both the Houses of
 Parliament on 14
th May, 2007.
2.         Action Taken Replies have been received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the 10th
 October, 2007 in respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report, which have
 been categorised as follows: -
(i)      Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry:

3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have
 been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item
 of Action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry.  The recommendations of the Committee
 contained in the One-Hundred and Sixteenth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and
 recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the
 succeeding paragraphs.
 
ASSESSMENT OF TENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN
(Recommendation at Para 6)
5.       The Committee appreciates that the Ministry of Civil Aviation has spent the allocated money to a
 satisfactory level except for the year 2006-07.  The Committee feels that the Civil Aviation sector has
 now become vibrant component of our economy and any laxity in utilisation of plan outlay can affect
 the development of the economy. The Committee ,therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Civil
 Aviation should ensure that all its organisations do utilise the allocated funds to the maximum extent in
 order to maintain its upper hand in the Civil Aviation sector where stiff competition is expected in the
 coming years due to the entry of more private players in the domestic and International arena.  The
 Committee hopes that this positive trend of utilisation of allocated outlay will continue during the 11
th
 Five Year Plan also.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6.       The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.   All efforts will be made
 for optimum utilisation of funds by all organisations under the Ministry during the XI Plan period.  
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
7.
                 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.

ASSESSMENT OF ANNUAL PLAN 2006-07 AND ALLOCATION FOR 2007-08
(Recommendation at Para 11)
8.       The Committee notes that except the Airports Authority of India, anticipated expenditure in
 respect of all other organizations is satisfactory. The Committee reiterates that the Ministry should
 ensure that all the organizations under its control utilize the approved outlay optimally.   The Committee
 desires that the utilization of external and internal budget resources for the acquisition of aircraft for Air
 India and Indian Airlines take place systematically.   The Committee also recommends that proper
 exercise should be done to identify the likely expenditure involved in the merger of Indian Airlines and
 Air-India and provision therefor should be made accordingly in the Budget at RE stage.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
9.       The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
10.
            The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.
 
 
AIR INDIA LIMITED
(Recommendation at para 19)
11.     The Committee notes that profit of Air India has gone down from Rs.96.39 crore to Rs.14.94
 mainly because of the reasons of appreciation in value of US dollar and increasing fuel price.   The
 Committee hopes that acquisition of new aircraft would certainly have positive impact on the operations
 of Air India. But still the Committee is of the view that Air India should adopt an aggressive marketing
 strategy to face the stiff competition at global level. The Committee is also of the opinion that more
 passenger friendly amenities be provided in its aircraft so that more and more passengers turn their
 interest towards the national carrier.  The Committee desires that the number of   bilateral agreements
 which were signed during the last year should be materialised to the maximum possible extent.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
12.     Air India is continuously making efforts to increase its revenues and profitability, as well as to
 compete with private sector airlines.   Some of the measures taken by Air India in the recent past are
 given below:
1)    They are proactively adjusting their pricing based on market demand and competitors'
 activities.
2)       In order to tap international traffic from interior points in India, Air India have tied-up with
 IC and are offering very attractive fares to such passengers travelling on IC domestic flights
 and connecting to Air India international flights.
3)    They have improved their schedules to offer convenient timings, non-stop flights,

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/125.htm[22-10-2018 12:28:24]
 standardised timings, daily departures and better connectivity to/from interior points in India.
4)    Kerbside check-in, lounge and special handling facilities are offered for high yield First and
 Business class passengers.
5)    To facilitate travel of passengers, facility of Advance check-in and City check-in are offered.
6)    Air India is in the process of acquiring 68 (including 18 for Air India Express) new  state-of-
the-art Boeing aircraft.   With the induction of the first two Boeing 777-LR aircraft, Air India
 has commenced non-stop services between Mumbai and New York (JFK).  The new aircraft
 will include luxurious seats for all classes, more luggage space and personal entertainment
 sets.
Future Plans:
13.     With the acquisition of additional aircraft, Air India will be expanding its network by operating to
 more destinations in USA such as San Francisco, Washington and Houston, as well as to other
 destinations such as Beijing, Australia, Mauritius, South Africa, etc.
14.     As soon as Air India obtains capacity for growth, it will increase its utilization of existing
 entitlements.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
15.     The Committee notes that the Air India is making efforts to increase its revenues and
 profitability as well to compete with private air operators and hopes that with the capacity growth
 and the utilisation of bilateral agreements, the profits of Air India will go up.  
 
INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED (IA)
(Recommendation at paras 26 and 27)
16.     The Committee notes that even though there is a substantial increase in the passenger load factor
 for the period from April to September, 2006, the profit of the IA seems to be declining. The physical
 performance of the Indian Airlines is showing good signs of improvement but it is not resulting in a
 good profit to the company.
17.     The Committee hopes that induction of new aircraft will help Indian Airlines to improve its
 profitability and the merger   of two national carriers will have a positive impact on the performance of
 both the Airlines.  The Committee feels that Indian Airlines should revamp its marketing strategies to
 get its due share in the domestic as well as in the international market and also to match with the
 services offered by the private operators.   The Committee also hopes that proper synergisation in the
 operation of Air India and Indian Airlines will have a positive impact on the performance of the Indian
 Airlines. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
18.     Physical performance of Indian Airlines for the year 2006-07 is given below and shows substantial
 improvement over previous years.

19.     During the month of May, 2007, Indian Airlines has achieved a passenger market share of 21.4%
 as compared to 21.3% of Jet Airways and 17.8% of Air Deccan.  IA’s also retained market leadership in
 RPK terms in May, 2007, being the market leader in RPK terms for the third month in a row, with a
 RPK market share of 21.7%, as compared to 20.8% of Jet Airways and 15.1% of Air Deccan.
20.     It is expected that with the induction of new aircraft into the fleet and with the merger of both
 Indian Airlines and Air India, the profitability of the merged entity would improve as a result of network
 synergies and cost savings.   As recommended by the Committee, marketing strategies will be
 formulated in order to increase the load factors on domestic and international routes and to match the
 services offered by competitors.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
21.     The Committee notes that there is very low margin between the passenger market share of
 Indian Airlines and its nearest competitor.  The Committee feels that the Indian Airlines can
 maintain its market lead only by initiating aggressive marketing and promotional strategies on
 priority. The Committee hopes  that adequate steps, in addition to the acquisition of aircraft, will
 enable Indian Airlines to tap the market opportunities in the domestic as well as the international
 markets.
 
AIRPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
(Recommendation at para 32)
22.     The Committee finds that the modernisation and expansion of some metro airports particularly of
 Kolkata and Chennai is also on hold for one reason or the other and privatised airports like Delhi are not
 giving the desired amenities to the air passengers.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
23.     As per the decision taken by the Government, modalities for expansion / modernisation of Kolkata
 and Chennai airport were to be decided in consultation with stakeholders including the State
 Governments of West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, respectively. Based on the outcome of the consultative
 process, it has been decided that modernisation / expansion of Kolkata and Chennai airports will be
 undertaken by AAI.
24.     AAI is in the process of finalising development plans for these airports, with a view to complete
 the expansion work by mid 2010. Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG) is finalising Action Plans in this
 regard. 
25.     Delhi airport, which has been restructured, is being modernised by JV Company in a phased
 manner. Master Plan for development has been finalised. It is expected that a new terminal building to

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/125.htm[22-10-2018 12:28:24]
 cater to 37 million passengers per annum will be operational by March 2010. A new runway and an
 interim domestic terminal building will be completed by mid 2008.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
26.     The Committee is constrained to note that the developmental activities of Chennai and
 Kolkata airports are still at consultation stage only.   Both Chennai and Kolkata airports are
 already overcrowded with the introduction of more services by operators to these airports and
 these air services are introduced without expanding or developing the existing infrastructure at
 these airports.  The Committee desires that modernisation programme of Chennai and Kolkata
 airports should be implemented on priority basis so that congestion at these airports is reduced to
 some extent.
(Recommendation at para  39)
27.     The Committee notes that the modernisation works undertaken by Airport Authority of India in
 the North-Eastern Region are progressing at a very slow pace.  The Committee recommends that works
 may be completed expediously so that airports in the North-Eastern States can be utilised fully as air
 traffic is vital for the people of North-East and also from the tourists' point of view.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
28.     It is submitted that high priority is accorded to upgradation of airport infrastructure in North-
Eastern Region and all efforts are being made to achieve the development targets. During financial year
 2006-07, AAI has spent Rs. 72 crores for capital works in N.E. Region against a target of Rs. 58 crores.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
29.
            The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.
 
(Recommendation at para  40)
30.     The Committee is disappointed to find that the condition of Patna airport which has already been
 declared as an International airport is far behind the standard of any International airport. The
 Committee recommends that efforts should be made by Airports Authority of India to provide such
 facilities at this airport as are available at the Airports at other countries like Singapore, Thailand, etc. 
 The committee further notes that development work carried out by Airports Authority of India in Gaya,
 Cooch Behar, Jaipur and Udaipur airports is very slow and recommends that all the works should be
 completed within a specified time frame at these airports. The Committee was informed by the Ministry
 that the Defence and environmental authorities have cleared the proposal of new airport in Cannore and
 the proposal has been sent to the Cabinet for approval.  The Committee is of the opinion that Airports at
 important tourist destinations should be modernised and all the amenities should be given to the
 passengers so that more tourists can reach these destinations by Air.   The Committee also feels that the

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

 development of non-metro airports should be completed by the end of December, 2009 so that the traffic
 pressure on the metro airports could be eased and these non-metro airports can be developed as major
 tourist destinations.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
Patna Airport:
31.     The development of Patna airport has been hampered due to certain constraints.  AAI has been
 constantly reminding State Government for cutting/ pruning of trees in the approach path of runway at
 Patna for smooth and safe aircraft landing and for a possible restoration of displaced runway threshold.As
 regards extension of runway, it is submitted that there is no scope for extension due to land constraints
 and obstructions in approach path on both sides of runway at Patna. AAI has proposed to construct apron
 for accommodating more aircraft and provision for Isolation  Bay subject to availability of land by the
 State Govt.
Gaya
 Airport:
32.     A new integrated Terminal Building has been completed with a capacity for 500 passengers at Gaya
 airport.   Construction of a new fire station Cat-VI has been completed. Extension of apron to
 accommodate two A320 and one B-737 and construction of Isolation  Bay is under completion. The
 location and drawings are being finalized for tender action for construction of new technical block cum
 control tower with modern air traffic management facilities.
Cooch Behar
 Airport
33.     The development works for Cooch Behar airport including runway extension/ strengthening for
 3700 ft & renovation of terminal building have been completed. The remaining 300 ft of runway
 extension work will be taken up after diversion of Mora Torsa stream at the end of runway by State Govt.
 The orders for demolition of identified structures/ buildings posing obstruction in the approach path are
 under issue by DGCA. The airport will be made operational as soon as above identified obstructions are
 removed by State Govt.
Jaipur & Udaipur Airports
34.     The progress of work at Udaipur and Jaipur was affected due to certain design related issues which
 cropped up during execution stage. However, these issues have now been sorted out and progress is
 being monitored closely so as to complete the work by December 2007 and March 2008 for Udaipur and
 Jaipur airports respectively.
Non-Metro Airports
35.     The development of 35 non-metro airports is proposed to be completed by the end of the financial
 year 2009-10.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
36.     The Committee is not satisfied with the pace of development of non-metro airports. The
 initial target for the development and modernisation of 35 non-metro airports is December,
 2009.   Now the target has been revised up to the end of the financial year 2009-10. The

 Committee is not satisfied with the explanation given for the delay especially in view of the
 unresolved controversy between the Government machineries on the development of the
 terminals and infrastructure of the non-metro airports. The Committee hopes that the new target
 date of development works of the non-metro airports will be adhered to so that the traffic at the
 metro airports is eased once non-metro airports are developed. 
(Recommendation at para  41)
37.     The Committee feels that Metro airports too require modernisation and expansion.  The
 Committee desires that the amenities available at the Delhi airport be verified to find out whether the
 agreed facilities to air passengers and air traffic are actually being provided or not and a status report be
 furnished to the Committee.  Modernisation of Kolkata and Chennai airports has separately been
 discussed in this report.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
38.     The provision of facilities, development of infrastructure etc. at the restructured Delhi and
 Mumbai airports is being monitored by the AAI in terms of the Operation Management Development
 Agreement (OMDA) entered into with the JV companies. An oversight committee, under the
 Chairmanship of Secretary (Civil Aviation), also periodically monitors the implementation of OMDA
 provisions.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
39.     The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry. The Committee, however, expresses its
 dissatisfaction on the pathetic facilities available to the passengers at Mumbai and Delhi airports
 and hopes new mechanism will ensure the improved amenities to the passengers.
 
PAWAN HANS HELICOPTERS LIMITED(PHHL)
(Recommendation at para 44)
40.     The Committee is of the view that PHHL can play a key role to provide air connectivity in North
 Eastern States and hilly areas where there is no possibility of laying big runways.  However, the
 Committee is constrained to note that PHHL which is the only PSU providing helicopter service in the
 country has failed to play its desired role effectively for which corrective measures have to be initiated
 on priority.  The Committee desires that funds allocated for purchase of machineries and other ground
 support equipments are utilized fully in 2007-08.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
41.     The recommendation of the Committee has been noted and PHHL shall endeavour to utilize the
 approved Plan Outlay optimally for acquisition of fleet and other major products in 2007-08.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
42.
            The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.

 Secretary of the Ministry is holding additional charge of CMD of PHHL which is affecting the
 functioning of PHHL.  The Committee desires that in the larger interest of PHHL a regular CMD

 w.e.f. 18.5.2007.

45.
            The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.
 
MERGER OF AIR INDIA LIMITED AND INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
(Recommendation at para 51)
46.     The Committee feels that the merger of these two national carriers would definitely result in
 proper synergisation of resources and enhance both financial and physical performance of both these
 carriers.  The Committee also feels that this process will help both the national carriers in long run in
 consolidating their position in domestic and international market.   The Committee hopes that the
 synergisation process would help to improve the operational efficiency of both the carriers. However,
 the Committee would like the Government to take care of the  interests of the employees in the new
 merged entity as merger of such large institutions always results in resentment amongst the employees
 as they are likely to lose their existing work position in the new merged entity.    The Committee notes
 the assurance given by the Government that there would be a three tier grievance cell to take care of the
 grievances of the employees of both the carriers after the merger. The Committee hopes that the
 mechanism of grievance redressal proposed by Government will be able to clear the doubts in the minds
 of employees.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
47.     Meetings were held with the Unions – even at the level of the Minister – to allay the
 apprehensions, if any, of the employees in the merger exercise.  The Chairmen & MDs of both the
 airlines have written to the employees explaining the rationale for the merger and assuring them that
 their interests would be protected and no employee would be worse off as a result of the merger.    
 Ministry has also in separate communications to the employees held out the same assurance.   The
 issues that may arise would be addressed on the basis of transparent and objective criteria and that a 3-
tier Grievance Redressal Machinery would be in place to address the employee grievances.   They have
 further stated that interaction with employee representatives would continue and their feedback would
 get due consideration. 
 

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
48.     The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  The Committee hopes that grievances and
 concerns of the employees of the both the organisations are addressed by the Ministry through the
 three tier Grievance Redressal Machinery.   The Committee hopes that the synergisation process
 of the Air India and Indian Airlines will be completed within the scheduled time and should have
 a positive result on the performance of these carriers.    
 
NATIONAL CIVIL AVIATION POLICY
(Recommendation at para 54)
49.     The Committee notes that the present civil aviation sector needs a well balanced and market
 oriented policy to address all the issues relating to the boom in passenger and cargo traffic.   The
 quantum of increase in passenger traffic needs strict enforcement of safety and security related issues. 
 The Committee, however, is constrained to note that Ministry of Civil Aviation has not come out with a
 Civil Aviation Policy till date. Now the Government plans to have a policy with a vision for 2020.  The
 Committee hopes that the policy will be in place soon and take care of all the issues relating to civil
 aviation sector of current as well as future era.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
50.     A Cabinet Note on National Civil Aviation Policy was considered by Cabinet in  its meeting held
 on 15
th June, 2007.  Cabinet decided that the matter may, in the first instance, be considered by a Group
 of Ministers.  Accordingly, a Group of Ministers is  considering the National Civil Aviation Policy. 
 Safety and security related issues have been kept in view and will be addressed in the proposed NCAP.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
51.     The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry. 
 
 RESTRUCTURING OF DELHI AND MUMBAI AIRPORTS
(Recommendation at para 56)
52.     While scrutinizing the outcome budget of the Ministry for the year 2006-07 the Committee finds
 that a substantial amount of money has been spent by the AAI for repair and maintenance work at
 international airports at Delhi and Mumbai even after these two airports were handed over to the JVCs
 in May, 2006.  The Committee desires to know the reasons for this and also wants to know the
 expenditure incurred by the JVCs on the respective airports for maintenance and up keep of airports till
 date.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
53.     The Outcome Budget for the year 2006-07 was only a projection in the event of delay in handing
 over of the airport by AAI to the JVC.
54.     The expenditure incurred by JVC for maintenance and upkeep of IGI Airport at Delhi  is Rs.33.92

 crores while the corresponding figure in respect of  CSI Airport at Mumbai is Rs.28.51 crores.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
55.
            The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.
 
(Recommendation at para  57)
56.     A Tripartite Committee with the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority
 of India and AAI Employees Joint Forum has been constituted by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on    
 22nd February, 2006 to look into the issues and proposals of modernizing airports by Airports Authority
 of India and employees related issues including job security.  The Committee desires to know the details
 of meetings which have been taken so far with the decisions arrived therein.   The Committee also
 reiterates its recommendation contained in its 106 th Report that the Tripartite Committee should hold
 regular meetings and finalise its Report in a time bound manner in view of the importance of the issues
 relating to the Committee.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
57.     The meetings of the Committee are held at regular intervals. The Committee has so far held 11
 meetings and various issues as stipulated in terms of reference of the Committee have been deliberated.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
58.
             The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  However, the Committee is unable to understand
 the reasons for the non-finalisation of the Report.
 
(Recommendation at para 58)
59.     There are also reports that after the work of modernisation of Delhi and Mumbai Airports has gone
 in the hands of private operators, the Ministry of Tourism even finding difficult to have space at the
 airports to display the publicity materials meant for information of the tourists particularly coming from
 abroad.  This gives an impression that there is a lack of coordination between the private operators and
 the Government agencies.   The Committee recommends that Government should look into the matter

 2007-08  also a budget provision of Rs.17.00 crores has been made for ACI.  Further, DGCA has been
 issuing NOC to new flying training institutes to take up training upto CPL level.   The NEC has a

 Aviation & Sustainable Tourism (FAST) has carried out a feasibility study with experts from the

UNIFORM TAXATION OF AVIATION TURBINE FUEL
(Recommendation at 69)
67.     The Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure and has direct bearing on the
 profitability of any airline. High cost of ATF in the country increases the cost of operation of carriers
 which results in escalation in the airfares.  The Committee recommends that Ministry of Finance should
 sympathetically  consider and give approval to the proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding
 notifying ATF as 'Declared Good' under Section 14 of Central Sales Tax Act on priority basis to all the
 aircraft  so that sales tax on ATF could be contained with the maximum rate of 4%. The Committee
 further recommends that the Ministry of Finance may also discuss the issue with the State Governments
 and try to persuade them to reduce the sales tax on ATF.  The Committee feels that restructuring the
 excise duty on ATF will have a positive impact on the development of civil aviation sector of the nation.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
68.     This Ministry has been requesting for rationalisation of taxes on Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) by

 cap the maximum rate of sales tax rate at 4%.  Ministry of Finance had earlier reduced sales tax on ATF
 for turbo prop aircraft to 4% by notifying it as ‘Declared Goods’.  Ministry of Finance, Department of
 Revenue has further amended the CST Act, 1956, through clasue 132 of the Finance Bill, 2007,
 including the ATF sold to an aircraft with maximum take off mass to less than 40,000 Kgs operated by
 scheduled airlines.   The recommendations of the Committee have been forwarded to the Ministry of
 Finance for taking appropriate action.  The progress in this regard will be reported to the Committee.

 the observations/recommendations contained in the Report.  These have been categorized as follows:-

 3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
 4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry of Tourism.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the One
 Hundred Nineteenth Report, action taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee
 on each item of action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
REVIEW OF ACTIVITIES OF THE TENTH PLAN (2002-07) AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN (2007-08)
(Recommendation at Para 8)
5.         The Committee is of the opinion that the plan outlay was not sufficient to exploit the tremendous potential of tourism

 in a sustainable and responsive manner which is short by Rs.210.50 crore and the utilization of funds under plan scheme of
 the Ministry has been as high as 92.74%. The budgetary allocation of the Ministry made for the entire 10th plan was not
 given to the Ministry of Tourism. The Committee strongly feels that any cut in the budgetary allocation will have negative
 impact on growth, strengthening of tourism infrastructure and hospitality related services in the country. The Committee
 expects that the Ministry of Tourism will strongly make demand for more allocation of funds for the 11 th Five Year Plan
 and will get the requisite funds for developing the tourism which is the sunrise industry of the day.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6.         The Ministry of Tourism has put forth  its demand of funds on the basis of 10% and 20% increase amounting to Rs.5405.58  
 crore and  Rs.6569.61  crore  respectively, as suggested by the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission is in the process
 of finalization of 11th Five Year Plan of Ministry of Tourism. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
7.         The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has placed its demand for more allocation of funds for the 11 th
 Five Year plan with the Planning Commission on the basis of 10% and 20% increase formula.  The Committee, however, is
 not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry.  The Committee feels that it seems the Ministry’s requirement of funds is
 minimal as they had opted for 10% and 20% increase.   The Ministry should have demanded more funds on the basis of
 their proposed requirement under various components and keeping in view the pattern of expenditure during the 10 th Five
 Year Plan justifying their demand for more allocation.   The Committee hopes that adequate budgetary allocation will be
 made to the Ministry of Tourism for the entire 11 th Plan period as per the projections for sustainable development of
 tourism products vis-à-vis strengthening of tourism infrastructure and hospitality sector in the country.
                       
(Recommendation at Para 11)
               8.      The Committee notes that during the year 2006-07, the Ministry of Finance imposed a cut of Rs.30 crore
 bringing it down from Rs.830 crore to Rs.800 crore at RE stage. The Committee is aware that the revised estimates
 are conveyed by the Ministry of Finance on the basis of the expenditure level upto 30
th September of the calendar
 year, and Ministry of Tourism was not able to utilize 50% of the budgetary allocation during 2006-07 till 30 th
 September, 2006. The Committee, therefore, desires the Ministry of Tourism to plan and incur their expenditure in
 a proportionate manner so that it is evenly spread throughout the year. The States/UTs may be continuously
 pursued to (i) send their proposals right at the beginning of the financial year, (ii) release funds to their Tourism
 Ministry or Department and furnish quarterly progress reports as well as utilization certificates of funds released
 in time by minimizing administrative and procedural delays in releasing funds.       
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
9.         The Ministry of Tourism plans to incur expenditure in a proportionate manner so that it is evenly spread throughout the year.
 For this the instructions of the Ministry of Finance for improvement in public expenditure have been circulated to all concerned for
 compliance and are being reviewed. The Ministry of Tourism has impressed upon all the States/UTs to send all their projects with
 requisite data and information well in time.  Also a system for online monitoring is being evolved. The status of the unspent
 balances lying with the States is regularly reviewed for every state and the states have been issued necessary directions to complete
 the projects and submit the pending Utilization Certificates/Completion Certificate expeditiously.         
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

10.       The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has circulated the instructions of Ministry of Finance to all the
 State/Union Territory Governments for improvement in public expenditure in a plan and proportionate manner.  However,
 the Committee feels that there is a need for putting in place a monitoring mechanism and minimising administrative and
 procedural bottlenecks to avoid delays.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to prioritize the projects and impress
 upon the concerned State/Union Territory Government for timely completion of projects.  This way time and cost overruns
 could be saved.
 
(Recommendation at Para 14)
               11.    The Committee is constrained to note that a large amount of unspent balances are lying with the States/UTs.
 Out of the releases made upto 31st March 2004, the unspent balances were Rs.184.37 crore as on 1st April 2005 and
 outstanding Utilization Certificates (UCs) were 397 which further went up to Rs.203.82 crore as on 31 st December
 2005 and outstanding UCs were 470. The cumulative unspent balance with States, for releases made upto 31 st
 March 2006, was Rs.542.09 crore. The Ministry’s contention that the amount shown as unspent is calculated on the
 basis of non-receipts of Utilization Certificates is untenable. The Committee feels that the Ministry has failed to
 gear-up the States/Union Territories and their machinery has not evolved effective system of planning and
 monitoring to do away with the procedural hurdles for timely completion of projects. Therefore, the Committee
 recommends the Ministry to impress upon the State/UT Governments to utilize all unspent balance lying with
 them on priority and furnish UCs so that the amount allocated for the entire duration of the 10
th Plan could be
 fully utilized. The Committee desires the Ministry to inform the Committee about the progress made in the matter.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
               12.    The Ministry of Tourism has impressed upon all the States/UTs to evolve a system of online monitoring with the
 help of NIC, and also to submit the interim reports for project implementation. The status of the unspent balances lying
 with them is constantly reviewed with   States/UTs and they have been issued necessary directions to complete the
 projects and also submit pending Utilization Certificates/Completion Certificate expeditiously. The status of pending
 UCs  is thus  being pursued vigorously.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
13.       The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry.   The Committee fails to understand as to why the
 Ministry is not evolving a fool-proof system of monitoring and review mechanism system for timely completion of tourism
 infrastructure projects.  The Committee feels that mere issue of administrative instructions to the States/UT Governments
 will not help much for creation of tourism infrastructure in the country.  The Committee may like the Ministry to be more
 pro-active and tie-up with NIC and State/UT Governments to evolve a system of online monitoring of utilization certificates
 and status of project implementation on their own.  The Committee recommends that the progress of various tourism
 related projects be monitored in the Ministry and funds should be released to the concerned State/Union Territory for
 completion of the projects.   The States/UT Governments may be constantly pursued to utilize all unspent balances lying
 with them and furnish utilization certificates for the projects sanctioned during the 10
th Plan period.  The Committee also
 recommends the Ministry to evaluate the existing scheme in the light of the outstanding utilization certificates and

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 53.      The recommendation of the Committee to set up a National Tourism Board has been re-examined in detail by the Ministry. 
 “The National Committee on Tourism” in its report submitted to the Government in 1988, taking into consideration the then
 prevailing circumstances, inter-alia, recommended the establishment of a “National Tourism Board”.  Since then, there has been a
 substantial change in the approach on the role of Government as provider of services to that of a facilitator and catalyst, particularly
 in sectors like Hospitality and Tourism.  It is true that tourism is a composite industry requiring coordinated efforts of several other
 Ministries and Departments and the State/UT Governments.  The implementation of tourism development projects and its
 promotion is primarily the responsibility of the State/U.T. Governments.  The Ministry is in full agreement with the observation of
 the Committee that inter-sectoral convergence of resources and policy integration is needed.   At present coordination is effected
 through established systems like inter-ministerial Committees constituted for specific purposes.  Besides the Committee on
 Secretaries chaired by the Cabinet Secretary takes up coordination and monitoring of issues at the highest level.   The Ministry of
 Tourism has also been included in the Committee of Infrastructure headed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister which enables better
 coordination on policy issues and monitoring for speedier implementation of major projects. 
 
54.       The earlier proposal to set up a ‘National Tourism Board’ as the principal arm of the Government for tourism sector with a
 Chairman at the level of Secretary to Government of India, with several full time members at the level of Additional Secretary
 assisted by three Additional Members at the level of Joint Secretary serviced by a number of technical officers and other staff

 subordinate manning a number of sub offices spread all over the country, is not in tune with the current thinking of a lean
 Government machinery.    Even if such a Board comes into existence, the Ministry of Tourism will have to exist, as the policy
 matters have to be essentially handled by the Ministry in the Government and not by a Board which is conceived as an executing
 field agency, outside the Ministry, vested with operational responsibilities. 
           
55.       Tourism related development programmes have to be essentially formulated and implemented by the State/U.T.
 Governments.  Even if a National Tourism Board is set up at the Centre, the State/U.T. Governments need not necessarily follow
 that pattern and they may continue to operate through their Departmental set up.  It may not be possible for the Central Government
 to direct the State/U.T. Governments to follow the central pattern, as tourism is not a subject matter which specifically appears in
 the Central list.  In the federal set up as in India, a Ministry rather than a Board at the Centre, would be a more effective mechanism
 to deal with a subject like tourism vis-à-vis the States/UTs.
 
56.       It may not be possible to draw a parallel between the Railway Board and the Tele-communication Board with the proposed
 National Tourism Board.   The Railway Board and Tele-communication Board provide specific services through their own agency
 throughout the country.  The proposed Tourism Board cannot be a service provider, as that of the Railway Board or Tele-
communication Board.  In the Tourism Sector, the institution at the Centre, whether it be a Ministry or a Board, is expected to be
 only a facilitator and catalyst, to promote tourism through the State/UT Governments and the private sector.  It cannot be the
 provider of services. 
 
57.       Matters like autonomy, operational flexibility, professionalism and better coordination can be addressed even in the existing
 framework without creating a separate Board.  The Directorate General of Tourism is the field organization under the Ministry of
 Tourism that can be further strengthened to meet with the emerging challenges and market demand. 
 
58.       The financial burden on a top heavy organisation can not be justified in the face of the changing role of the Government.  
 The Railway Board and the Telecommunication Board generate their own revenue whereas the Tourism Board would not be in a
 position to generate such revenues.  It will have to depend heavily on budgetary support.   If that is the case there does not appear to
 be any major advantage in setting up a National Tourism Board. Therefore, in the given circumstances when the Government is
 keen to contain administrative expenditure the proposal to create such a Board is considered to be neither essential nor desirable.  
 What is required is the capacity building of existing machinery and further empowerment through delegation of authority and
 moderanisation for better coordination and cost effective performance.

NATIONAL HIGHWAY  DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (NHDP):
(Recommendations at Para 41 and 42)
21.       The Committee expresses concern over the fact that there are 7 stretches of Golden Quadrilateral still pending; out
 of these, four stretches are of more than 50 kms in length.   It indicates a sorry state of affairs that Golden Quadrilateral
 project which was scheduled to be completed by the end of 2003 have extended over four more years and now stretched
 upto 2007-08.  Still, the Department has not chalked out strategies to deal with contract defaulters or legal wrangles.  The
 Committee also notes that five road stretches of N-S Corridor and E-W Corridor are also pending. The Committee
 strongly recommends that all these works should be completed at the earliest.
22.       The Committee notes that 94.77% of the Golden Quadrilateral Project has been completed by February, 2007. 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the slow progress of this project and rescheduling of target of completion of
 the project more than 5 years. Though the Department of Road Transport and Highways has enumerated a number of
 steps taken to ensure early completion of the NHDP, like monitoring of contracts at various level, appointing of nodal
 officers by State Governments, constitution of Committee of Secretaries, simplification of procedure of land acquisition,
 action against non-performing contractors and improving cash flow problems of contractors. However, when it comes to
 the implementation of the projects, it appears that things have not improved. The construction of flyover at Delhi -
 Badarpur border can be sighted as an example as how the procedural hurdle delaying in projects leading to cost overrun
 and time escalation.   The project was approved by the Department of Road Transport and Highways on 31
st March,
 2005, however the project is yet to be finalised for want of a number of clearances. This project forms part of Golden
 Triangle of Agra, Delhi and Jaipur where lakhs of domestic and foreign tourists visit on it. The project could have been
 taken on priority basis particularly taking into account in the Commonwealth Games, 2010. The Committee recommends
 that the steps enumerated by the Department for the early completion of the project should be implemented in letter and
 spirit so that there is not cost overrun and time overrun. The Committee hopes that the Department would take necessary
 precautions in future while finalizing such type of projects which require huge amount of investment.   In this context the
 Committee reiterates its recommendation made in the 102
nd Report that "proper verification of bank guarantees
 submitted by contractors should be undertaken at the initial stage itself to avoid termination of the contracts at a later
 stage.  The Committee notes that increasing numbers of contracts are under implementation and being awarded. 
 Therefore, it is recommended that the Department should be vigilant in respect of each contract and should strictly
 enforce the compensation conditions in the contracts in respect of non-performing contractors. The Committee, further,
 recommends that the Department should not wait for the targeted date of completion to initiate action but should fix
 short-term targets for the contractors so that the projects can be monitored constantly and immediate and early remedial

30.       The procedure for conformation of bank guarantee has been streamlined.   The officials have been directed that
 before opening the financial proposals (in case of bid security), signing of the contract (in the case of performance
 security), release of payment (in case of bank guarantees for mobilization advances / against retention money), etc as the
 case may be:
a)
                  The confirmation from the issuing branch of the bank is obtained in writing through registered post /
 speed post / courier.   The bank should be advised to confirm the issuance of the bank guarantee (s)
 specifically quoting the letter of NHAI on the printed official letter-head of the bank indicating address
 and other details (including telephone Nos) etc of the bank and the name, designation and code number of
 the officer(s) confirming the issuance of the bank guarantee;
b)
                  Confirmation is also obtained with the help of a responsible officer (not below the rank of Manager) at
 PIU / HQ, which is close to the issuing branch of the bank who should personally obtain the confirmation
 from issuing branch of the bank and forward the confirmation report to the concerned Technical Division
 at HQ;
c)
                  As a matter of abundant precaution, the confirmation from the controlling office of the bank may also be
 separately obtained by the concerned Technical Divisions.

QUALITY CONTROL:
(Recommendation at Para 51)
38.       The Committee desires that there is a need for indigenization of norms regarding designing of roads and bridges
 taking into account the local site conditions.  The Committee hopes that there should be uniform norms / guidelines in the
 country for highway projects.   The Committee recommends that an independent agency should be appointed to monitor
 and inspect the quality of all works carried out by both the Governmental and also the private agencies. There are reports
 that Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi has made third party checks mandatory by a panel of institutes
 i.e., Delhi College of Engineering, CRRI and IIT Delhi for all road works like strengthening and resurfacing.   The
 Committee desires that the Department may also involve similar mechanism to check the quality of repair work carried
 out on the National Highways and this independent audit should be made part of the contract while awarding it which
 will also ensure that works carried out are at par with international standards or norms.
Reply of the Government:
39.       Design codes /  manuals / standards and Ministry’s Specifications for Road & Bridge Works, 2001 (4
th Revision)
 published by Indian Roads Congress are indigenous and take into account the local site conditions. The specifications are
 evolved keeping in view the international norms and practices. As far as National Highway projects are concerned,
 almost uniform norms / guidelines are followed throughout the country incorporating certain changes warranted by local
 site conditions.  In order to ensure the quality, various executing agencies, viz, National Highway Authority of India
 (NHAI), State Public Works Departments (PWDs), Border Roads Organization (BRO) have quality control system in

 place.  For projects under National Highways Development Project, NHAI has engaged supervision consultants to ensure
 the quality of its roads / bridges according to desired standards / specifications for National Highways.  For NHAI
 projects, quality audit is also being done by Engineers India Ltd, a Government of India Undertaking.   Overall quality of
 work is also monitored as a double check at construction sites by NHAI’s Project Implementation Units (PIUs). To
 ensure quality, normally, there are provisions in the contract agreement that in case any work is not found conforming to
 the prescribed technical standards / specifications, the action will be taken by the engineer for rejection / replacement /
 rectification of work / material.  Further, generally there is also a provision of minimum 12 months defect liability period
 after the completion of the period during which it is the responsibility of the contractor to rectify the defects, if any. 
40.       In response to Committee's specific question regarding mandating the third party check for monitoring and
 inspecting the quality of works carried out by the governmental and private agencies, the Department has stated that the
 execution of development works on National Highways are being carried out on agency basis through National
 Highways Authority of India (NHAI), Border Roads Organization (BRO) and State Public Work Departments.
41.       NHAI had appointed Engineers India Ltd., Central Road Research Institute and Gujarat Engineering Research
 Institute as independent auditors for quality audit for the works carried out on the Golden Quadrilateral, North-South and
 East-West Corridor and Port connectivity projects.   Further, they have also appointed M/s TUV SUD South Asia Pvt.
 Ltd. as third party Independent Quality Auditors on 14.12.2007.  The firm is in the process of completing the agreement
 formalities and shall be starting the quality audit work shortly.
42.       Quality audit is being considered for SARDP-NE projects.   The monitoring of quality of works will be got done
 through individual experts to be engaged through India Roads Congress.  Further, reputed institutes such as IITs will be
 involved for conducting tests and materials and works being executed by the contractor.
43.       It has also been decided to appoint third party independent quality auditors for National Highway  works and State
 road works funded from CRF being implemented by State Governments.  The details of appointment and the check list
 etc. are being finalized. BRO is executing the work departmentally in difficult terrain/strategic areas.  There is apparently
 no need for a separate quality audit of works handled by BRO.
 
Further recommendations/observations of the Committee
44.       The Committee appreciates the decision of the Department to appoint third party independent quality
 auditors for National Highway works.  The Committee hopes that this measure may help in ensuring qualitative
 execution of National Highway works.

TOLL TAX ON BRIDGES AND NATIONAL HIGHWAYS:
(Recommendation at Para 104)
81.       The Committee is not convinced with the reasons advanced by the Department of Road Transport and Highways
 for collecting toll on roads and bridges in perpetuity.   The Committee feels that the Government is not justified in
 burdening the common users of highways with the development as well as the maintenance of the roads in the country. 
 The Committee had also commented upon this matter in its 67 th Report on Demands for Grants 2003-04 and
 recommended that once the cost of construction of a road/bridge plus interest is recovered, the collection of toll should be
 stopped. The Committee also feels that there exists a need for the rationalisation of the toll tax being charged on the
 National Highways.  The Committee recommends that persons travelling on smaller stretches of the National Highways
 where toll is being collected should be charged a lower amount than the persons using the entire length of that National
 Highway.   The Committee also recommends that a one time revolving fund should be set up for all the major road
 projects in which share of road projects from CRF should be kept.  The Committee also expresses its concern over the
 multiple-taxation on the vehicle owners by way of tax on the time of purchase of vehicle, cess on purchasing of
 petrol/diesel and collection of toll when he uses tolled highways.  The Committee sees no logic behind such multiple-
taxation on vehicle owners.  The Committee recommends that on BOT Annuity basis contracts, the concessionaire should
 be prevented from collecting toll once he recovers his capital and interest on the project.
Reply of the Government:
82.       Huge amount of resources are required for development and maintenance of National Highways. Considering the
 quantum of available resources, it was decided by the Government to charge user’s fees in perpetuity.  This was a change
 from the previous policy of discontinuation of collection of user’s fees after the cost of the bridge along with interest was
 recovered.  The financing of seven phases of NHDP is based on continuation of user’s fees in perpetuity.
83.       In the open toll system, rationalization of fees is not possible because monitoring the distance travelled by the
 users is difficult.  However, concessions to the local users are also given.
84.       Present levy of cess is tied up for the implementation of NHDPs and Prime Minister’s Gram Sadak Yojana and the
 improvement of sanctioned works of State Road.  Therefore, it may not be possible to create a revolving fund until and
 unless the amount of cess is increased.  However, this is being taken up with Ministry of Finance.
85.       A massive programme for development of National Highways in the country has been launched called the
 National Highway Development Programme (NHDP).   The aim of the programme is to provide world class road
 infrastructure in the country.  Improved road infrastructure will result in considerable savings to the road users by way of
 reduced vehicle maintenance cost, reduced travel time etc.  The implementation of various phases of NHDP requires
 massive investment which cannot be met by public funding alone.  The present rate of cess is Rs 2 per litre of both petrol
 & diesel and are being utilized for development of all categories of roads in the country. Therefore, the fund available
 from cess alone is insufficient to cater the need for development. Therefore, several ways of funding like external
 assistance from the foreign financial institutions, tapping of internal resources, cess on petrol & diesel and users fees
 have been explored.  The financing of the NHDP will be affected if user’s fee is discontinued, unless the level of cess is
 increased.  The tax levied on purchase of motor vehicles is collected by State Government.
86.       Under the BOT annuity basis contracts, the collection of users’ fees is done by the Government.   Annuity
 payments are made to the concessionaire to reimburse his cost of construction.  The amount received by the Government
 as users’ fees are considered in the financing structure of the project.
87.       The private sector participation which is the major sources of financing for NHDP Phase-III to Phase-VII is based
 on the collection of Users' Fees by the private entrepreneurs.  Therefore, the Users' Fees is being collected on perpetuity
 basis as a source of financing for development and maintenance of National Highways.
 
Further recommendations/observations of the Committee
88.       The Committee is not satisfied with the replies of the Government.  The Committee reiterates its earlier
 recommendations and feels that there is no reason to collect users' fee in perpetuity.  Once the capital and interest
 is recovered, the users' fee must be discontinued.  The creation of a revolving fund may be further pursued with
 the Ministry of Finance.

APPRAISAL OF THE 10
TH PLAN AND THE ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2007-08
(Recommendation at Para 10)
5.       The Committee is distressed to note that during the 10 th Plan, the Department of Shipping was
 allocated Rs.2570.89 crore as budgetary allocation under the plan scheme which was reduced to
 Rs.1700.00 crore at the RE stage. The Committee does not see any merit therein and strongly disapproves
 the idea of reduction of plan outlay because once it is reduced by the Government at the beginning of the
 Five Year Plan itself it will certainly affect and jeopardise many of the plan activities of the Department.
 The Committee is further constrained to note the shortfall in utilization of funds in almost all the major
 activities of Department of Shipping i.e. Inland Water Transport, Shipping, Ports, Lighthouses and
 Lightships, Shipbuilding etc. During 2005-06, the utilization of funds was Rs.346.83 crore against RE
 Rs.405.00 crore, in 2006-07, the utilization of funds was Rs.510.21 crore against RE Rs.575.00 crore and
 Rs.759.00 crore has been allocated for BE 2007-08. The Committee is aware that the main reason for
 effecting reduction in funds at RE stage by the Ministry of Finance is the inability of the Department of
 Shipping to spend their allocated funds during the first two quarters of almost every year.  The Committee
 observes that the major portions of the budgetary outlay had been utilized during the last two quarters of
 the financial year by the Department. The Committee disapproves the practice as the funds crucial for the
 development of Shipping and Port Sectors infrastructure are withheld in the process. The Committee

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/128-1.htm[28-08-2018 13:26:12]
 notes that the reasons advanced by the Department for non-utilization are administrative in nature for
 which corrective action could have been taken in advance. The Committee, therefore, recommends the
 Department to plan and incur their expenditure in a proportionate manner so that it is evenly spread
 throughout the year so that the funds are utilised  appropriately for the purposes and no alibi should be
 provided to the Ministry of Finance to reduce the allocations at the RE stage.
 
Reply of the Government
6.       Utilization of plan outlay primarily depends upon as to how quickly the execution of project has
 been approved by the Competent Authority.  Depending upon the nature and estimated cost of the project,
 the project is required to be appraised by the Appropriate Appraisal Forum before obtaining the approval
 of the Competent Authority.  Sometimes, compliance of this procedural requirement takes time resulting
 delay in execution of the project.  To ensure optimum utilization of funds, token provisions are now being
 kept at the time of preparation of Budget Estimates (BE) in respect of those projects which are yet to be
 approved by the Competent Authority.   In the case of projects which have already been approved by the
 Competent Authority and allocation has been made in the Annual Plan,  the financial & physical progress
 of all such projects are now being regularly monitored   at the highest level in the Department of
 Shipping.  This monitoring has now yielded desired results and during the year 2006-07, the Port Sector
 has utilized Rs.336.16 crores against the allocation of Rs.476.12 crores in Budget Estimates thereby
 achieving a utilization of 70.60% which is the highest in any one year of entire 10 th  five year plan
 period.  In respect of Revised Estimates of Rs.363.83 crores, the utilization percentage was 92.39%. 
 
7.       As regards, the reasons for getting the delayed approval of competent authority, the Department of
 Shipping in response to the question on ATR submitted that the need for obtaining ‘in principle’ approval
 of the Planning Commission before a project is included in the Annual Plan of a Department has been
 dispensed with subject to these projects fulfilling certain prescribed criteria.  Based on these criteria, most
 of the projects in the Shipping, Inland Water Transport and Port Sector would not require ‘in principle’
 approval of the Planning Commission.  This is expected to result in significant saving in time involved in
 the appraisal and approval process by facilitating concurrent processing of project proposals for approval
 alongwith the exercise for firming up the plan allocations.   Further, the threshold limit for obtaining
 approval of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs for Plan projects has been increased from
 Rs.100 crore to 150 crores.
 
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
 
8.       The Committee notes that in order to ensure optimum utilization of funds token provision are being
 kept at the time of preparation of budget estimates for projects/schemes for which approval of the
 competent authority is yet to be received.    The Committee recommends the Department should continue
 to work out strategy for maximum utilization of plan outlays and prioritize the projects in consultation
 with the concerned agencies for better co-ordination and timely execution of the projects.
 
(Recommendation at Para 11)
9.       The Committee also recommends that the Department of Shipping should do away with procedural
 hurdles and maintain close liaison for the purpose of review, monitoring, implementation and co-
ordination of programmes /activities. The Committee hopes that Department of Shipping would take all
 corrective steps in this regard to avoid shifting of focus from the shipping sector in the next plan.

 (CoS), Public Investment Board (PIB) or Public Private Partnership Appraisal Committee (PPPAC) as the
 case may be], depending upon the nature and estimated cost of the project before obtaining the approval
 of the Competent Authority.  However, the following measures which have/are being taken are expected
 to streamline the procedures, reduce hurdles & expedite the projects.:-
 
(i)
                Major Port Trusts have been delegated powers to incur plan expenditure upto Rs.50 crores in
 case of additions/modifications/new investments and Rs.100 crores in case of
 replacement/renewal of assets. Within these delegated powers, the Major Ports make investment
 decisions.  A proposal to enhance the financial powers to the Port Trusts is under consideration.  
 
(ii)
                   The Department of Shipping has taken up a proposal for waiver of the requirement of
 obtaining ‘in principle’ approval from the Planning Commission for projects included in the
 National Maritime Development Programme and also the projects which appear in the Annual
 Plans. The Planning Commission vide their Note N-11016/4/2006-PC dated 29.08.2006
 informed that “In Principle” approval for existing schemes is not required provided the scheme
 have been evaluated as a part of the Zero Based Budgeting (ZBB) evaluation process. In case of
 new schemes/projects which are proposed to be taken up and have been indicated in the Plan
 documents, “In-Principle” approval of Planning Commission would not be required provided
 financial resources have been fully provided for.
(iii)
            A proposal to permit the Port Trusts to appoint Project Management Consultant in a project in
 anticipation of sanction of the project, is under consideration of the Department of Shipping,
 with a view to saving time.
 
(iv)            A Model Concession Agreement (MCA) for PPP projects in the Major Ports is under
 formulation.  On finalisation, PPP projects in the Major Ports which follow the MCA will be
 exempted from obtaining ‘in principle’ clearance from the PPPAC, which is, otherwise required
 before commencing the bidding process for the project.
 
(v)              The threshold limit for posing PPP projects for clearance by the PPPAC has been raised from
 Rs.100 crores to Rs.250 crores by the Government after considering the delays that would result

 Shipping.
 
(vi)            The Department of Shipping has set up a Committee for standardization of documents and

(vii)          Review and monitoring of implementation of programmes/ activities are carried out on a regular

13.     The Committee notes with concern that the budgetary allocation under the Plan scheme for port

th Plan had been slashed down

 of the Department of Shipping. In BE 2006-07, an outlay of Rs.1364.25 crore comprising of Rs.476.12
 crore as gross budgetary support was provided to the port sector and Department of Shipping had been
 able to utilize Rs.1024.53 crore or 75% of the budgetary allocation during the year. The Committee is

14.     Full utilization of budgetary allocation could not be made in the Tenth Plan Period because

 formulation, appraisal and approval of projects funded through public investment have been laid down by
 Ministry of Finance.   The Department of Shipping is making all efforts to ensure optimum utilization of

 This has led to a perceptible improvement in utilization of funds.  In the Port Sector, the total expenditure
 in the first year of the Tenth Plan viz. 2002-03 was Rs. 541.89 crores comprising Rs. 40.13 crores as

 utilization in respect of GBS at 70.60%. 
 
15.     The constraints explained by the Department for slow progress in providing infrastructural facilities
 at various Islands in Lakshadweep are factual.   These schemes could not progress as per schedule on
 account of constraint of transporting material which in fact is the main problem. 
 
16.     The total area of Lakshadweep Islands is 32 sq Km and these four Islands are very small having area

 entire construction material is taken from the main land, sometimes in pre-fabricated condition.  All
 vessels carrying materials are kept at sea and the offloading is synchronized for construction purpose. 
 The ships cannot come alongside the Islands due to low draft and corals.  Another reason is the prolonged
 rainy season from April to October during which construction cannot be carried out as the sea and the
 weather is not conducive for construction or transportation of materials.
 
17.     To compound matters recently, waves of 6-6.5 meters hit the jetties of Kavaratti  and Minicoy on
 16.5.2007 causing damage to the forward section.  The question of raising the height of these jetties under
 construction in all the 4 Islands from present 4.5 to 5 meters from Sea level along with appropriate
 designed breakwater for safety of ships has been mooted by Administration of UT Lakshadweep.   The

 merged entity, the worst victim of non-implementation of merger process who had been acting-brain of
 RBD's operation since its nationalization. The Committee recommends the Government to take steps to
 ensure that the remaining 57 employees are also taken into the pay-roll of GRSE as decided by the
 Cabinet.
                  
Reply of the Government
87.     The decision of the Government regarding Rajabagan Dockyard (RBD) is as follows:
                   "Handing over of Rajabagan  Dockyard (RBD) along with its existing manpower (371
 employees), assets and liabilities to Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) or to
 any other PSE an outright purchase/ long terms lease/management contract basis in a
 transparent manner to be overseen by a group of Secretaries." 
 
88.     Accordingly, RBD stands transferred   along with its existing manpower of assets and liabilities to
 Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) w.e.f. 01.07.2006. Out of 371 employees listed  
 proposed for transfer to GRSE, 50 employees opted for Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS),  5 
 employees left due to superannuation, death etc. and two employees opted to remain with the
 Corporation. In this way, M/s GRSE Ltd. had finally absorbed 314 employees out of 371 employees.
 
Further recommendation/observation of the Committee
89.     The Committee notes the reply and recommends the Department of Shipping to vigorously pursue the
 matter with the Ministry of Defence  to ensure absorption of the remaining 57 employees of Rajabagan
 Dockyard (RBD) with Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd. (GRSE) as per the decision of the
 Cabinet.
 
(Recommendation at Para 80)
90.     The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of its recommendation in the past, the Government
 has not come out with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of River Service
 Division (RSD). The Committee is of the opinion that CIWTC with its infrastructure and expertise can
 play an integral part for development and promotion of inland water transport through NW-1 and NW-2.
 The Committee recommends that possibility may also be explored to physically amalgamate the
 remaining CIWTC with Inland Waterway Authority of India (IWAI) or Kolkata  Port Trust (KoPT) or
 Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), so that the infrastructure and expertise of CIWTC can be utilized for
 development of waterways transport.
                                                                                     
Reply of the Government
 
91.     The Corporation has about 100 IWT vessels out of which 40 are operational. While some of the
 non-operational vessels are awaiting repair some are beyond economic repair. A detail exercise on
 deployment of the vessels of the corporation is underway. A few vessels of CIWTC have been given on
 dry charter as well. CIWTC operated 47 voyages in NW-1 between 2004 and 2006 at the behest of IWAI.

 as Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), Kolkata Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of

 waterways for propose of Shipping and navigation and for matter connected therewith or incidental
 thereto. Thus the role of IWAI is not of an inland water operator/commercial organization. Merger with
 KoPT also was not found feasible. SCI operates only ocean going ships and does not operate in inland
 waterway vessels. Hence merger of CIWTC with SCI was also not found feasible.

 consideration of the Government as on date for revival of CIWTC with existing assets.  The Cabinet vide

TH AND 11 TH FIVE YEAR PLANS AND OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF FINANCIAL
 PERFORMANCE FOR THE YEARS 2006-07 AND 2007-08:
 (Recommendation at Para 5)
5.         The Committee notes that while comparing B.E. 2006-07 and B.E. 2007-08, it is observed that most of the major
 schemes under the Ministry of Culture have got increased allocations. The Committee feels that preservation and protection of
 vast cultural resources of the country is a task gigantic in nature and requires huge investments. But, the Committee is at dismay
 that the Government has always treated it as non productive sector thereby inviting apathy of the Finance Ministry which is
 always reducing the allocations made for the Ministry of Culture at Revised Estimates stage. The Committee strongly feels that
 this sector is catalytic for economic growth and not only that but also preservation of our culture means preserving our national
 identity which should not be compromised at any cost. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the allocations made for the
 year 2007-08 should not be reduced at RE stage by the Finance Ministry and the Ministry of Culture should try to spend the

 allocations to the fullest extent.
 
 
 
(Recommendation at Para 10)
6.         Our culture is the most vibrant and rich culture in the world. The Committee feels that culture has to be harnessed
 together with tourism and showcased to the world. The right modal mix between culture and tourism would yield valuable
 foreign exchange by inviting more and more tourists; promote our artists and artisans many of whom are at the verge of
 starvation; preserve our local regional culture, art and craft ; last but not the least, it will also enthuse private sector to invest
 more and more in these activities. The Committee strongly recommends that the approach of the Ministry of Culture, Ministry
 of Finance and Planning Commission should change during the 11th Five Year Plan and all of them should together take
 adequate care and ensure that none of the Plan activities in respect of Ministry of Culture and its organizations is deferred due to
 reduction in Annual Plan outlay at the stage of Revised Estimates.
 
(Recommendation at Para 13)
7.         The Committee strongly recommends its earlier observations with regard to budgeting pattern of the Ministry of Culture
 and reiterates its recommendations made at para 11 of the 103
rd Report on the Demands for Grants for the year 2006-07 wherein
 it was stated that:
 
"The Committee is of the view that fixing of the Revised Estimates ceiling by the Ministry of Finance on the basis of the
 level of expenditure attained upto the month of September/October creates problem for the Department of Culture. The
 Committee observes that most of the cultural functions and festivals take place in the month of October and November,
 after the monsoon. The Archaeological Survey of India also incurs major expenditure after the monsoon. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends that Government must review the budgeting procedure and evolve some mechanism
 to ensure that the Plan allocation for the Department of Culture is not reduced. The Committee recommends that if the
 review of the budgetary allocation is done in the month of December, instead of the month of September then the cut in
 the budgetary provision could be avoided”.

 forwarded to Ministry of Finance and to the Planning Commission for appropriate action at their end.

9.         The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  The Committee further observes that the matter of reduction of
 Annual Plan Outlay at RE stage has been taken up  with the Planning Commission  and Ministry of Finance.  The
 Committee recommends that the Ministry should vigorously pursue the matter and the Committee may be informed of

 CULTURE:
(Recommendation at Para 16)
 
10.        The Committee notes the sorry state of affair prevailing in various premier institutions of art, culture and literature and
 several of them are functioning headless.  The Committee takes strong exception to the fact that Screening Committee is not
 meeting regularly.   The Committee is also surprised to notice the lethargic approach of UPSC towards filling up these vacant
 posts which should have been done rather without any loss of time.   The Committee therefore, recommends that the Ministry
 should propose an amendment to the rules and a composite method of recruitment should be followed instead of direct
 recruitment method.   The Committee strongly feels that these key posts should be taken out of the purview of the UPSC and
