Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
28.  The Committee notes the reply and would like to know the grant of subsidy, unit-wise both for the PSU and for the 
non-PSU shipyards during the above period, and also  whether any further suggestions have been received  from the 
beneficiaries to the revised scheme. 
Port Sector  
29.  The Committee finds that the total allocation for ports sector during 2009-10 under both plan and non-plan was Rs.700.03 
crore. Out of this amount, Rs.279.l1 crore only the  Ministry was able to utilize up to February, 2010 which is close to 40 % of 
the total allocation. This slow pace of programme i mplementation is a matter of serious concern. Alrea dy our port carriage is 
negligible compared to the global capacity. Time bo und completion of projects not only controls cost e scalations but also the 
revenue earning directly and indirectly as a result  of increased imports and exports. The Committee th erefore recommends that 
the Ministry should have a clear picture of the pro grammes to be implemented during the financial year  with the allocated 
grants. 
      (Para 22 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
30.  In the year 2009-10, an expenditure of Rs. 275 .51 crore out of total allocation of Rs. 385.50 cro re as GBS has been 
utilized. The percentage of expenditure is 71.46. S imilarly, an amount of Rs. 325.23 crore out of tota l allocation of Rs. 529.21 
crore in the year 2009-10 (Non-Plan) has been utili zed. The percentage of expenditure is 61.45. For Se thusamudram Ship 
Channel Project, an outlay of Rs. 151.10 crore was kept in the year 2009-10. Due to non-approval of Revised Cost Estimates of 
the project and also order of Hon’ble Supreme Court  for suspension of Work not a single paisa was incu rred in the year. This 
was the main reason for incurring less expenditure in the year 2009-10. . 
31.  In the year 2010-11, an outlay of Rs. 388.48 c rore as GBS has been allocated for Port Sector. The  main allocation has 
been made for Capital Dredging Projects of Cochin a nd Tuticorin Ports. Besides this, allocation has al so been made for Post 
Tsunami Works, Various Studies, IT for Department o f Shipping and purchase of Survey Vessels etc. Simi larly, an amount of 
Rs. 535.58 crore has been kept in Non-Plan Budget f or the year 2010-11. The main allocation has been m ade for Maintenance 
Dredging Project in Haldia and Kolkata Port Trust, ALHW (Estt.), Major Works of ALHW and Tariff Regula tory Authority of 
Major Ports. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
32.  The Committee notes that despite the efforts made b y the Ministry, they have only 71.46% out of the to tal 
allocations which was to be spent. At the same time , various projects are lagging behind due to shorta ge of funds and 
such a situation is a matter of great concern. The Committee, therefore, recommends that all out effort be made for the 
maximum utilization of funds.  

Ports-Major and Minor  
33.  The Committee is of the view that the ports pl ay a major role in the economic development of the country. The 
Committee, however, notes that the major ports of the country are already facing stiff competition from the ports of neighboring 
countries particularly from Srilanka and Singapore. Now, development of private and minor ports are ta king away the business 
of Major ports. This according to the Committee is clear reflection of the manner in which the Governm ent are handling the 
affairs of the Major Ports, wherein the crore of ru pees of tax payers have been invested. The Committe e recommends that the 
Government should ensure level-playing field for the Major Ports so that they can perform and compete with private and minor 
ports, In this connection the Committee would like to reiterate its earlier recommendations contained in its 134 th  report which is 
reproduced as below:- 
“The Committee notes that the Department of Shippin g is in process of formulating a Maritime Policy fo r the maritime 
sector which seeks to ensure a coordinated developm ent of Ports, Shipping, Inland Water Transports, Sh ip building and 
Ship repairing with the objective to upgrade and mo dernize the port infrastructure in India to benchma rk its performance 
against global standards. The Committee also gather ed from the replies that the regulatory authority w ill be set up at an 
appropriate time. The Committee observes that since much of the activities in the port sector are taking place with private 
participation there is need to establish regulatory authority well in time and that too before coming across any problem for 
better control, coordination and monitoring for ach ieving excellence in the port and shipping sector b esides addressing 
serious security implications. The Department to ta ke steps for setting up of a regulatory on the patt ern of Telecom 
Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) and Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (ARDA) for creating a level 
playing field and foster healthy competition and to  encourage investments for the shipping and port se ctor besides 
monitoring performance standards and adjudication of disputes and disposal of appeal thereof.” 
      (Para 27 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
34.  This para makes the following recommendations:  (A) “Government should ensure level playing field for the Major Ports 
so that they can perform and compete with the private and minor ports...” 
35.  It may be mentioned that private ports are und er the jurisdiction of respective State Government and are beyond the 
jurisdiction of the Tariff Authority for Major Port s (TAMP). However, within the policy framework-atte mpts are made to 
encourage the ports for increasing the operational efficiencies and make use of economies of scale. The Ministry has also made 
efforts to simplify the procedures for approval of various projects of Ports on Public Private Partner ship (PPP) basis. Recently, 
the Ministry has removed the cap for short-listing the bidders at Request for Qualification (RFQ) stag e for increased 
participation. Further, the Ministry of Finance has  also delegated more powers to the Administrative M inistries for giving 
approvals for the project. Now, projects up to Rs.3 00 crores need not be sent to the Cabinet for appro val. All this will lead to 
speedier implementation of the projects in major po rts. Separately, a high level committee has made ce rtain recommendations 
for increasing the port efficiency and the policy reviewed for major ports. . 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
36.  The Committee notes the reply. The Committee is of the opinion that in view of increasing number of pr ivate 
ports, the performance of the PSU ports needs to be looked into and necessary support be provided. The Committee may 
be informed about the recommendations of the high l evel committee for increasing port efficiency and t he action taken 
by the Government thereon.  
37.  The Committee appreciates the performance of m inor ports, whose cargo handling has grown up from mere 5 per cent in 
1999 to 35 per cent of total cargo handling in 2009 . This only implies that Government’s policy has no t allowed major ports to 
grow and therefore, is losing business. The Governm ent themselves admitted that minor ports offer bett er facilities, cargo 
clearance and other formalities in a hassle free manner. 
      (Para 28 ibid ) 
 

Reply of the Government  
38.  Since several Non-Major ports have come up alo ng the coastline with private investment, traffic h andled at these ports 
has also increased. These ports are under the jurisdiction of the respective State Governments, as per the Indian Ports Act 1908. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
39.  The Committee is of the view that the rate of cargo  handling capacity growth is far greater in the cas e of private 
ports than that of Major Ports. The Major Ports should get adequate attention and policy support from the Government 
to improve their efficiency and competency.  
40.  The Committee is of the view that this is high  time when the ports within the country both major & private should be 
developed in an integrated manner so that they can unitedly compete with the port of neighbouring countries. 
      (Para 29 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
41.  For a better understanding and coordinated dev elopment of Non-Major ports along with major ports,  Maritime State 
Development Council (MSDC) is functional. Ministry of Shipping holds meetings every year in which the representatives of 
Major Ports as well as State Governments participat e and exchange their views. Based on discussions he ld at various meetings 
of Maritime States Development Council (MSDC), several steps have been taken for integrated. development of port’s capacity. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
42.  The Committee desires to know the major decisions a rrived at and executed by the MSDC. Lack of adequat e and 
effective coordination between the State Sector Por ts and Major Ports is conspicuous. The Committee fe els that only 
through a co-ordinated and prompt action, the port sector could sustain in this era of globalization a nd privatization 
and efforts may be made in this direction.  
43.  It was brought to the notice of the Committee that some major countries give exclusive coastal sh ipping rights to their 
vessels. The committee, therefore, recommends that while considering the demand of the foreign vessels for cargo shipping the 
interests of the Indian vessels and Indian Shipping Industry should be fully protected. 
      (Para 30 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
44.  The observations/recommendations of the Hon’bl e Committee have been noted. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
45.  The Committee is at dismay to note that the Ministr y has not given any concrete steps to protect the I ndian 
Shipping Industry. The Committee, therefore, reiter ates recommendation that while considering the dema nd of foreign 
vessels for cargo shipping, the interests of the Indian Shipping Industry should be fully protected. 
International Container Transhipment Terminal (ICTT)  
46.  The Committee is of the view that the Internat ional Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) Project is one of its kind in 
the world and it would not only boost the maritime position of India, the cargo handling capacity of t he country will also 
increase considerably, once the project was fully o perationalised. The Committee is, however, concerned to note the slow pace 
of work of the Vallarpadam transshipment terminal. The Committee notes that the commissioning of the ICTT has been delayed 
due to one reason or other. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should prevail upon their own contractors 
and coordinate with concerned Government agencies like NHAI to ensure that all the necessary facilities are constructed in time 
for the operationalization of the ICTT, with utmost priority. 
      (Para 36 ibid ) 
 
 

Reply of the Government  
47.  The Ministry of Shipping has been vigorously m onitoring the Project regularly. With regard to sup porting infrastructure 
projects of the ICTT Project i.e.  Rail connectivity, road connectivity and capital d redging, the progress is being regularly being 
monitored by the Ministry. Secretary (Shipping) has reviewed the project with the Chairman of Cochin P ort and the officials of 
the various agencies concerned. The Ministry has ta ken up the matter w.r.t.  road connectivity with Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways under whose administrative control NHA I functions. NHAI has undertaken the work on deposi t basis. It is 
expected that two way lane connectivity would be fully operational by October, 2010. The work of rail connectivity project has 
been completed and it is ready for operationalization. For the project of Capital Dredging, sufficient funds are being provided to 
the port. In the current year also an outlay of Rs.  237.97 crore has been allocated. It is expected th at operation of ICTT would 
commence in October, 2010. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
48.  The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry and likes to point out a discrepancy in the reply furnished by 
the Ministry about the operational Date of the ICTT  being October, 2010 while the reply was submitted to the 
Committee on 22nd November, 2010. It seems the Ministry is not aware of the ground realities and is not sure whether it 
is operationalised or not. The Committee may be inf ormed about the latest status of operationalisation  of various 
projects at ICTT. 
Shipping Corporation of India (SCI)  
49.  The Committee is happy to know that the impact  of global recession has started diminishing and the global economy is on 
revival path. The Committee recommends that SCI should review its planned activities and fix the targets accordingly to ensure 
that its profit is increased. The Committee notes that for the year 2010-2011, an amount of Rs. 2921.37 crore has been provided 
for vessels on firm order and an amount of Rs. 1064  crore has been provided for new projects of acquis ition of vessels and 
investment in joint ventures. The Committee hopes t hat the SCI would make all out efforts to utilize t he amount optimally and 
implement its programmes to acquire more vessels, without further loss of time.   
      (Para 46 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
50.  While SCI is already in the market for acquiri ng second hand resale vessels to get benefit of the  lower prices in view of 
recent stabilizing of the market. SCI has initiated  its new building vessels acquisition proposals als o. In this respect SCI has 
already floated separate tenders for acquisition of  2+2 very large crude carriers and 4 Nos. Karnsarma x Bulk Carriers. These 
tenders are in addition to the tenders floated for second hand/resale superamax bulk carriers and container vessels. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
51.  The Committee notes the reply given by the Min istry. 
Requirement of Cargo Ships and Oil Tankers  
52.  The Committee observes that there is a shortfa ll of 96.3% and 83.6% in the carriage of cargo capa city and carriage of 
POL/Liquid cargo capacity respectively. Presently, the foreign vessels are enjoying almost 90% of Indi an Cargo business. The 
Committee observes that quite a large number of cargo vessels are more than 25 years old and that dry cargo like iron ore which 
is a major component of die Indian export could not  be carried by these old vessels. The Committee is of the view that if the 
steps are not taken to augment the fleet capacity in general cargo/container segment and tanker tonnage, the carriage capacity of 
India may further diminish in the coming years. The  Committee, therefore recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should 
prepare concrete plans and arrange for resources to  build/procure more vessels. The Committee notes th at an amount of 
Rs.3985.37 crore has been provided in the budget es timates during 2010-11 for acquisition of vessels b y SCI. The Committee 
hopes that with the acquisition of above ships by the SCI, carriage capacity of Indian shipping sector will get a major boost. 
      (Para 54 ibid ) 
 

Reply of the Government  
53.  SCI is keen to achieve its targets of acquirin g 37 more vessels by the end of 11 th Five Year Pla n which will not only 
boost SCI’s tonnage and market share but will also improve the share of Indian lines in carriage of India’s Overseas trade. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
54.  The Committee notes the reply and would like t o emphasize the need for expediting the vessel acquisition.  
Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL)  
55.  The Committee noted the activities carried out  by DGLL. The Committee observes that the pattern of spending during the 
previous years are not up to the mark. The Committe e hopes Ministry of Shipping will keep check to ens ure timely 
implementation of the plans by the Directorate General of Lighthouses & Lightships (DGLL). 
      (Para 56 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
56.  In the Annual Plan 2009-10 an outlay of Rs.40. 00 crores as GBS had been provided to DGLL out of w hich the 
Directorate has utilized Rs.37.52 crores. The remaining amount could not be utilized because environment clearance in some of 
the projects was not received. Similarly, in the An nual Plan 2010-11 an outlay of Rs.60 crores has bee n provided out of which 
the Directorate has utilized 6.89 crore in the firs t month of the Annual Plan itself. The observations  of Committee has however 
been noted and implementation schedule will henceforth be monitored periodically. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
57.  The Committee notes the reply and emphasizes the ne ed for obtaining whatever clearances are required f or a 
project before making budgetary provisions to such projects. 
Indian Maritime University  
58.  The Committee notes that the Indian Maritime U niversity was set up on 14th November, 2008 in Chen nai. IMU is the 
first and only Maritime University in the country. The Committee, however, notes an apparent lack of s incerity on the part of 
the Government in expediting the establishment of t he University. It is evident from the fact that for  want of approval and 
clearances from the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) and Cabinet Committee on economic Affairs (CCEA), an amount of 
Rs.53 .80 crore allocated in BE 2009-10 was reduced  to Rs.5.53 crore at the RE stage. The Committee ho pes that the 
Government will accept the demand of a sum of Rs. 2 82 crore required for over a period of time for the  development of 
infrastructure. The university has the Headquarters  in Chennai and the headquarters building and the c ampus have to be 
developed. Another new campus is coming up in Cochi n apart from other campuses in Kolkata, Mumbai and Visakhapatnam. 
Additional classrooms and hostel facilities also need to be developed for implementing the OBC reservation in these campuses. 
Apart from that, the new courses are also being int roduced and so, the allocation demanded is for capi tal expenditure. The 
Committee is also aware of the fact that there is a  great shortage of trained and skilled manpower in maritime sector. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should make all possible efforts to start new cou rses and augment the 
number of students intake in the premier marine institutes. The Committee strongly recommends that adequate additional grants 
may be given for the above programmes. 
      (Para 63 ibid )

59. The Government has established Indian Maritime University (IMU) on 14/11/2008 in Chennai with campuses at Chennai,

62.  The Committee is of the opinion that keeping in vie w the various deficiencies pointed out to the Commi ttee from 
time to time, further planning for expansion of the university need to be relooked and operationalized. 
Inland Waterways Authority of India  
63.  The Committee notes that an allocation of mere  Rs.115 crore has been made for the IWAI for the ye ar 2010-11. The 
Committee is of the view that the amount is inadequ ate even to meet the maintenance of the existing op erational waterways. 
Since this allocation was not sufficient even for o ngoing projects of National Waterways 1, 2 & 3, eff ectively no fund will be 
available for the new National Waterways, except token provision of Rs. 1 crore each for NW 4 & 5. The Committee also notes 
the facts presented by the Ministry that the total cost of development of National Waterway 4 is of th e order of Rs. 1500 crore 
and that of National Waterway 5 is of the order of Rs. 4200 crore. If both these projects were to be completed in a period of 5-8 
years, it is estimated that Rs.5700 crore would be required for taking up development of these two wat erways. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends the Planning Commission to pr ovide this amount during remaining two years of the  11th Plan and the 
12th Plan. It need to give required priority/import ance to the development of National Waterways. Dema nds and proposals 
made by the Ministry of Shipping for development of  waterways need to be taken more seriously and maki ng a drastic cut on 
the fund projected by the Ministry should be avoided. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should take up 
the matter with the Ministry of Finance and the Pla nning Commission for increased allocation for the d evelopment of National 
Waterways. 
      (Para 72 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
64.  The observations and recommendations of the Ho n’ble Committee are noted for compliance. The matter has already been 
taken up with Planning Commission at the highest level in March, 2010 for allocation of Rs.500 crore for development of these 
two newly declared National waterways so that activities could be initiated during the 11th Plan period. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
65.  The Committee may be informed about the progre ss made in this regard. 
Central Inland Waterways Transport Corporation (CIWTC)  
66.  The Committee is constrained to note that desp ite being recommended a number of times, the Govern ment has not been 
able to come up with a package for the revival of C IWTC. In this connection, the Committee would like to invite the attention 

of the Government to the recommendations of the Committee contained in 117th Report on Demands for Grants, 2007-08 of the 
Ministry of Shipping which is reproduced below:- 
“The Committee is constrained to note that inspite of its recommendation in the past, the Government h as not come out 
with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of River Service Division (RSD). The Committee is of 
the opinion that CIWTC with its infrastructure and expertise can play an integral part for development  and promotion of 
inland water transport through NW-I and NW-II. The Committee recommends that possibility may also be e xplored to 
physically amalgamate the remaining CIWTC with Inla nd Water Transport Authority of India (IWAI) or Kol kata Port 
Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) , so that the infrastructure and expertise of CIWTC  can be utilized 
for development of waterways transport.” 
67. The Committee would like to reiterate its earli er recommendation contained in its 134th Report on Demands for Grants 
(2008-09) of the Ministry of Shipping which is reproduced below:- 
“The Committee is pained to note that the Governmen t has decided neither to consider revival of CIWTC nor to 
amalgamate this Corporation with various Organizati ons, such as Inland Waterways Authority of India (I WAI), Kolkata 
Port Trust (KoPT) or Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) that too, without getting conducted any scien tific study by an 
expert agency. The Committee is of the view that th e matter of revival and amalgamation of CIWTC shoul d be got 
examined by some high powered expert committee.” 
68.  The Committee recommends that in a democratic welfare State, interest of employees and their live lihood must find 
uppermost consideration, while taking a decision which is adversely affecting them. Before taking fina l decision with regard to 
the viability of CIWTC the Committee again recommen ds that the matter may be got examined by a high po wer expert 
Committee and job security and livelihood of the employees must be ensured.   
      (Paras 78, 79 & 80 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
69.  A Committee is being set up in the Ministry to  examine the matter. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
70.  The Committee may be informed about the composition  of the committee formulated for the purpose, its t erms of 
reference and the targeted date for its submission of recommendations. The recommendation of the committee may also 
be submitted to the Committee. 
Taxation and Tax Reliefs  
71.  The Committee feels that the port and shipping  sector of the country had not received the attenti on in the Union Budget 
2010-11 that it surely deserves. No incentives, con cessions, tax relief etc. to the Ports and Dredging  Sectors or to the Shipping 
Industry has been announced. The Committee is of th e view that extending the infrastructure status to the shipping sector will 
make them also accessible to some of the tax exempt ions and subsidies as enjoyed by other agencies which will give a boost to 
the shipping industry. The other demands raised by the Ministry are also hold ground and accepting them is necessary to attract 
investment in the shipping sector. Cruise shipping is a long pending demand in the tourism sector and tax exemptions really will 
be a welcome step. The Committee, therefore, recomm ends that the above demands may further be pursued with the Finance 
Ministry to get positive results. 
      (Para 83 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
72.  In the Budget Memorandum dated 4.12.2009 we ha d requested Finance Ministry that certain long pend ing tax related 
issues need to be addressed so that level playing f ield is available to Indian Shipping Industry. Thes e demands included (i) 
Exemption from payment of Minimum Alternative Tax ( MAT) on profit on Sale of Vessels (ii) Exemption fr om Corporate 
Income Tax on Interest Income on funds deployed out of tonnage tax reserve (iii) Exemption of Indian Seafarers from payment 

of Income Tax (iv) Exemption for Major Ports from p ayment of Income Tax (v) Exemption of Cruise Shippi ng from the net of 
service tax and custom duty on bunkering (vi) Exemption of Dredging activities from the net of service tax.  
73.  Further to above, an another letter dated 12.2 .2010 was sent to Finance Ministry with the request that certain issues which 
are adversely effecting the growth of Indian Shippi ng Industry may be considered for inclusion in the Union Budget. These 
were: (i) Removal of Service Tax on Dredging (ii) R ail Road connectivity for Ports (iii) Inclusion of profit on sale of vessels 
within tonnage tax regime (iv) Inclusion of interes t income on funds deployed out of tonnage tax reser ve within tonnage tax 
regime (v) Grant of infrastructure status to shippi ng and shipbuilding industry and (vi) providing dut y free bunkers for coastal 
shipping. 
74.  Although, none of the above demand of the ship ping industry has been addressed in the Union Budge t 2010-11 but this 
Ministry continues its efforts to convince Ministry  of Finance for redressal of above long pending dem and of the shipping 
industry. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
75.  The Committee would like to see response of the Min istry of Finance to these demands. Therefore, the c omments 
of the Ministry of Finance on the proposals of the Ministry of Shipping may be furnished to the Committee. 
Safety Measures for Ships  
76.  The Committee feels that safety and security o f the seafaring vessels need to be given paramount importance, especially 
in view of the increasing piracy and theft of cargo . This also has relevance in view of the increased threat from terrorists who 
are active in our neighbouring seas. The Committee,  is however constrained to note that an amount of R s. 48.96 crore which 
had to be reduced to Rs. 12 crore at RE stage for w ant of utilization of funds by the Ministry of Defe nce. The Committee also 
notes that no justification has been given for not accepting the demand of Ministry of Defence for Rs.  100 crore for the survey 
vessels. The Committee would like to have an explan ation in the matter. The Committee is of the view t hat the action of the 
Government to reduce allocation to Rs. 15 crore for  safety and security of the vessels is a retrograde  step. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry of Shipping may be pro vided with adequate fund at the RE stage to meet th e actual threat and 
challenges in this regard. 
      (Para 87 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
77.  The final allocation of Rs. 15 crore for BE 20 09-10 was made by the Ministry of Finance. However,  based on the 
recommendation of 156th Parliamentary Standing Committee to provide more fund at RE stage, a provision  of Rs. 10 crores of 
additional allocation was made in the RE of 2009-10 on the request of Ministry of Defence, but the entire additional fund of Rs. 
10 crores lapsed by the end of Financial Year 2009- 10 because Ministry of Defence did not send their request for release of the 
amount despite repeated intimation to them for sending their proposal for the same. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
78.  The Committee is surprised to know that Ministry of  Defence did not respond despite repeated requests from the 
Ministry of Shipping. As a result the amount lapsed . The Committee would like to know the reasons from  the Ministry 
of Defence.  
79.  The Committee also opines that in the recent t imes, the shipping industry is facing an increased challenge from piracy and 
sea robbery. This is great threat to maritime navig ation resulting in cargo loss, man power loss and i ncreased operational costs. 
There should be some strong measures to save the cargo ships and sea men from such anti pirates. Keeping in view of the above 
facts the Committee strongly is of the views that lack of funds should not be a problem in this regard the allocation may be kept 
with an open mind because the safety and security of the ships and the persons who are working in it are of utmost importance. 
      (Para 88 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  

80.  Indian Navy has deployed one warship since Oct ober, 2008 to patrol the Maritime Security Area in the Gulf of Aden. 
Indian ships along with foreign ships with Indian S eamen are informed to take advantage of the presenc e of the warship. India 
is also actively participating in the meetings of t he UN-supported Contact Group on piracy which consi sts of five international 
organization, viz . African Union, EU, NATO, UN Sectt. and IMO and 22  countries who have an interest in protecting the GOA 
Sea link. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
81. The committee appreciates the steps taken by the Go vernment and recommends that we should be contently  vigil 
against piracy. 
Dreding of the Hooghly River System  
82.  The Committee notes that the Kolkata Port was incurring revenue losses mainly due to drop in dept h of the navigation 
channel that prevents large ships from venturing in to the Haldia dock. Due to decline in traffic movem ent, the earnings of the 
dock have reduced significantly. Considering that t he Kolkata Port is one of the major ports of the co untry, the situation 
prevailing is not at all healthy for the sector. 
      (Para 89 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
83.  The depth in the Haldia channel has been deter iorating gradually for the last few years. Though l arger ships are regularly 
entering the Haldia Dock, parcel load of cargo has reduced due to reduction in the navigable depth. 
84.  It is a fact that due to decline in traffic mo vement, the earning of the dock has reduced signifi cantly. The Ministry has 
taken steps to improve the draft situation at KoPT/ HDC. DCI has already been directed to deploy adequa te number of dredgers 
at Kolkata Port Trust/HDC. KoPT has taken various d evelopment projects to overcome the problem caused due to declining of 
draft in Haldia Channel. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
85.  The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry . The Committee also wanted to know the progress ma de so 
far in the dredging activities and targeted date of completion of the deepening works.  
86.  The Committee notes that dredging of the Hoogh ly river system is very essential for the survival of the Kolkata Port 
system. The Committee also notes that the policy of reimbursement of 100% of the cost of dredging by the Central Government 
has been referred to the Cabinet for a fresh mandate. The Committee recommends that the Central Government should continue 
to reimburse the entire cost of the dredging at Hal dia River system and the related Channels as the Ko lkata Port is not in a 
position to bear the cost.  (Para 91 ibid ) 
 
Reply of the Government  
87.  Recommendation of the Committee accepted for c ompliance subject to Cabinet decision on continuati on of dredging 
subsidy to Kolkata Port Trust. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
88.  The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry . The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the 
Central Government should continue to reimburse the  entire cost of dredging at Haldia river system and  the related 
channels as the Kolkata port is not in a position to bear the cost. The recommendation of the Committee may be brought 
to the notice of Cabinet and it may be persuaded to  take a favourable decision to continue the 100% re imbursement of 
the dredging cost of Haldia river system and related channels.  
89.  The Committee notes that the warehousing infra structure in respect of Kolkata and Kandla ports is  not able to meet the 
current requirements. Even though other ports have sufficient capacity as on date, keeping in view the  Ministry’s plan to 

enhance the carriage capacity of ports and other measures of port development, once fully operationalised, the required capacity 
may be increased. Therefore, the warehousing infras tructure is also an important field where the Minis try should concentrate 
along with the other capacity augmentation methods. (Para 94 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
Kolkata Port Trust  
90.  The present warehousing facilities both at Kol kata Dock System (KDS) and Haldia Dock Complex (HDC ) are sufficient. 
At HDC, construction of a new warehouse of 5000 Sq.  mtrs. has been started and the same is going to pu t in use from April, 
2011. Continuous upgrading in respect of storage ar ea, roads and other infrastructure inside port acco rding to the trade 
requirement is being made both at KDS and HDC. 
Kandla Port Trust  
91.  Kandla Port is regularly constructing new godo wns and open plots to meet the cargo storage requirements. So far, the port 
has constructed 271 godowns in 121 lakh Sq. mtrs. ( open area). The port has also developed two C.W.C. operated Container

92.  Based on the present traffic levels and the ex pected growth in throughput, it is felt that Kandla  Port is geared to meet not 
only the present traffic levels, but also the additional traffic growth in the coming years.

93.  The Committee notes the replies given by the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that the storage facilities 
in Major Ports need not only be increased but also to be made more clean and secure as much of the cargo should not be 
in the open for long time.

Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
97.  The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry . The Committee hopes that the projects already awa rded 
would be completed in time.  
98.  The Committee also feels that Indian ports nee d to be modernized at the earliest so that with the  arrival of modern 
equipments in the ports, the port capacity will con siderably increase along with increase in cargo mov ements. The Committee 
feels that consequently, the profitability increases and in a phased manner the cargo handling cost fa ctor and the capacity factor 
could be brought at par with the international levels. Thus the problem of poor infrastructure and high levels of manual handling 
of work could be managed in a better way.    
  (Para 96 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
99.  Up-gradation and modernization of port infrast ructure is essential to benchmark the performance o f Indian ports against 
global standards. The Government of India has given the top priority to the Modernization of ports, which is undertaken through 
various expansion/up-gradation projects for berths,  Construction of new berths/terminals, Installation  of new and modem 

equipment, Up-gradation/replacement through higher capacity of cargo handling equipment and Mechanizat ion of cargo 
handling operations.  
100.  Mechanization of cargo handling facilities is  of utmost importance for improving the efficiency of ports. Introduction of 
high capacity mechanized equipments in the form of mobile harbour cranes/floating cranes etc. through the private sector 
participation, with a view to utilizing the latent capacity, as well as for augmenting the cargo handl ing capacity of major ports 
would go a long way in reducing the handling cost o f cargo at the major ports and will also increase t hroughput substantially. 
All Major Ports have, accordingly, taken up and planned several projects for modernization for capacity augmentation. 
Further Recommendations/observations of the Committee  
101.  The Committee noted the reply given by the Ministry . The Committee observes that modernization measures may 
definitely enhance the cargo handling capacity of t he Indian ports however, the pace of the work need to be improved 
considerably.

INTRODUCTION  
  I , the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture, h aving been 
authorised by the Committee to present on its behal f, do hereby present this One Hundred Sixty Fifth R eport on “Action Taken 
by the Government on the Recommendations/Observatio ns of the Committee contained in its One Hundred Fi fty Seventh 
Report on Demands for Grants 2010-2011 of the Ministry of Culture”. 
2.  The One Hundred Fifty Seventh Report of the Dep artment-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on  Transport, 
Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the 22nd April, 2010. 
3.  The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations  of the Committee contained in its One Hundred Fift y Sixth Report 
were received from the Ministry of Culture on the 24th November. 2010. 
4.  The Committee considered and adopted the Report  at its meeting held on the 20th December, 2010. 
 
 
 
  SITARAM  YECHURY 
 
NEW DELHI ; Chairman,  
December  20, 2010 Department-related  Parliamentary Standing  
Agrahayana 29 , 1932 (Saka)  Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture. 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
REPORT  
1.The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on observations/recommendations as contained 
in its One Hundred Fifty Seventh Report on Demands for Grants (2010-11) of the Ministry of Culture, wh ich was presented to 
the Parliament on 22nd April, 2010.  
2.  Action Taken replies was received from the Gove rnment on 24th November, 2010, in respect of all th e 
observations/recommendations contained in the Report. The Replies have been categorized as follows:- 
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been acc epted by the Government: 
 Para Nos.12, 35, 53, 58, 75, 82, 95, 104, 112 and 126 
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committ ee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government replies: 
 Para Nos. 29, 33, 37, 38, 40, 41, 49, 50, 63, 92, 106, 121 and 134 
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich replies of the Government have not been accepte d by the 
Committee: 
 Para Nos.16, 17, 18, 29, 30, 32, 45, 51, 52, 57, 6 1, 62, 72, 81, 84, 88, 105 and 120  
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of whi ch final replies of the Government are still awaited: 
 Para Nos. Nil 
3.   The Committee desires that final replies in re spect of the recommendations, which have been categ orized as interim 
replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest. 
4.  On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Co mmittee has made observations on each item of the action taken/proposed 
to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the One Hundred Fifty Seventh Report, action 
taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of acti on taken have been 
given in the succeeding paragraphs. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
5.  The Committee underlines the need for more allo cation to the Ministry of Culture lest many of its important activities 
should suffer. For the year 2010-11, the Ministry of Culture has been allocated an amount of Rs.735 cr ore, which comes to less 
than 12 paise per hundred rupees being spent under the General Budget. However, the Committee is surpr ised to find that 
during the first three years of the Eleventh Five Y ear Plan, the Ministry as in the past has not been able to utilize even the 
reduced allocation. Under-utilization of funds by the Ministry of Culture is a recurring phenomenon ye ar after year. During the 
year 2009-10 the allocation of Rs. 700 crore was re duced to Rs. 630.00 crore at RE stage, however, the  Ministry could utilize 
only an amount of Rs. 533.40 crore. The Committee r ecommends that the Ministry should identify the bot tlenecks and make 
corrective measures to utilize the allocations as per the norms laid down for the purpose.    
         (para 12 of the 157th Report ) 
Reply of the Government  
6.  During the year 2009-10, as against Plan alloca tion of Rs.700.00 crore which was reduced to Rs.630.00 crore at RE stage, 
the Plan expenditure of Rs.573.79 crore has been in curred upto 31.03.2010 which constitute about 91.08 % of RE 2009-10. To 
utilize the entire Plan allocation, in the beginning of the current financial year, the Ministry reviewed the last year’s expenditure 
position in light of the short coming in achieving the optimal utilization of Plan funds and identifie d various bottlenecks. To 
make corrective measures to utilize the allocations , the Secretary (Culture) had addressed a D.O. lett er dated 03.05.2010 
instructing all the Cultural Organizations and Divisional Heads under the Ministry of Culture for suitably phasing the budgetary 
expenditure, especially under Plan, from the very b eginning of the financial year so that the expendit ure is incurred in an even 
manner to meet the required financial target first by the end of September, 2010 and also by the end of March, 2011. In addition 
to this, the Ministry has taken a decision regardin g release of grants in two instalments of 75% and 2 5% to Autonomous 

Organizations/Grantee Institutions to enable them t o plan their activities well in advance and for bet ter expenditure 
management. These remedial measures will help in optimal utilization of Plan funds during the current financial year 2010-11. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE.  
7.  The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and h opes that the Ministry would be able to optimally u tilize the 
resources in 2010-11.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
8.  The Committee notes the comments of the Ministr y of Finance. However, the Ministry of Finance/Plan ning Commission 
has not offered any solution to the problem of the Ministry of Culture which the Committee still appre ciates, The Committee 
deplores the “one size fits all” attitude of the Mi nistry of Finance and recommends that the non-utili zation of funds due to the 
hostile weather and season may be given a special s tatus to ensure that allocation is not reduced at R E stage. Till there is no 
respite on this account, the Ministry of Culture wi ll have to make efforts to maximize this expenditur e before the review of the 
RE allocation begins.    (Para 16 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
9.  The above recommendation has been referred to M inistry of Finance and Planning Commission for taki ng appropriate 
action thereon. The ATR will be submitted on receipt of final reply from MoF and Planning Commission. 
10.  In order to maximize the Plan expenditure befo re review of the RE allocation begins, the Secretar y (Culture) had already 
addressed a D.O. letter dated 03.05.2010 instructin g all the Cultural Organizations and Divisional Hea ds under the Ministry of 
Culture for suitably phasing the budgetary expendit ure, especially under Plan, from the very beginning  of the financial year so 
that the expenditure could be incurred in an even manner to meet the required financial target by the end of September, 2010. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
12.  The Ministry should also explore new methodolo gy for conservation and preservation with the help of 
Scientists/Universities which can be done in all-we ather conditions. The Committee observes that the f und allocated to ASI 
need to be given a special status to make it non-lapsable.  (Para 17 ibid ) 
 
Reply of the Government  
13.  In addition to traditional methods of conserva tion and preservation Archaeological Survey of Indi a is open to new 
methodology wherever it is found essential. We have  requisite interactions with Scientists/Technocrats  of 
IITs/NITs/CBRI/SERC and other reputed institutions. Workshops/Seminars are being conducted regularly to update the skills of 
conservation professionals. It will be much useful if funds allocated to Archaeological Survey of India are made non-lalpsable. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
15.  The Committee once again recommends to the Min istry of Finance and the Planning Commission to understand the needs 
of the institutions working under the Ministry of C ulture and the limitations of those institutions to spend the money during the 
first six months of the financial year.  (para 18 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
16.  The above recommendation has been referred to Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission for tak ing appropriate 
action thereon. The ATR will be submitted on receipt of final reply from MoF and Planning Commission. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
17.  Reply in response to Committee’s recommendation con tained in para 16 and 18 is disappointingly casual.  Merely 
passing on its recommendation to Planning Commissio n and Ministry of Finance and waiting for reply ref lects an 
attitude which needs to be guarded against, if we w ant to improve the things. The Committee would like  to know when 

these recommendations were forwarded to the Plannin g Commission and Ministry of Finance and what their  response 
is.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
18.  The Committee notes the excavation work in var ious places and recommends that every care be taken  to ensure that the 
time schedule prescribed for each of the excavation work is adhered. (Para 29 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
19.  The excavation/exploration work proposed by Ar chaeological Survey of India (ASI), State Archaeolo gy Departments, 
Universities and Research institutions is being giv en permission on yearly basis i.e. for every field season Proposals for 
exploration/excavation are called every year and ar e placed before the Standing Committee (SC) of Cent ral Advisory Board of 
Archaeology (CABA) for recommendation. The licence issued by ASI for carrying out the scheduled exploration/excavation by 
various agencies is valid till 30th September every  year. The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sit es and Remains Act, 
1958 clearly mentions under Chapter III (Constructi on and other Operations in Protected Area) under Ru le 14 (Period of 
Licence) which mentions “Every liecnce shall be in force for such period not exceeding three years as may be specified in the 
licence: Provided that the Director General may, on  application made to him at least one month before the expiry of a licence, 
extend its period by one year at a time so that the  aggregate period does not exceed five years”. For this field season (2010-
2011) proposals for exploration/excavation have bee n received by ASI and shall accordingly be recommen ded/ not 
recommended by the SC of CABA. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
20.  The Committee is not convinced with the reply that gives only procedural details and no account of tim e schedule 
of the excavation work carried on has been given.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
21.  The Committee recommends that ASI should explo re new scientific methods to preserve and conserve the heritage sites. 
The major research and scientific institutions may be roped in to explore newer technology and scienti fic knowledge for 
preservation and conservation of heritage sites. (para 30 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
22.  In the conservation of heritage structures tra ditional methods and techniques take precedence over the others. However, to 
incorporate new technology for conservation/preserv ation of monuments we have taken the services of II T Delhi, IIT Kanpur, 
lIT Chennai, NIT Warangal, CBRI Roorkee, Survey of India Dehradun, IISC Bangalore, SERC Chennai and ma ny other 
scientific institutions. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
23.  The Committee would like to know, if any standard n ew technique has been developed for different kinds  of 
heritage sites, or it is taken on case to case basis.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
24.  The Committee is of the view that there is a n eed for publications in archaeology for general awa reness in all the major 
Indian languages, besides some foreign languages, t hese publications should aim at creating interest i n the public about our 
ancient monuments and archeological sites as well t he importance of preserving these as our cultural h eritage. Such awareness 
in the general public would facilitate better protection/maintenance of these sites.  (para 32 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
25.  Archeological Survey of India brings out publi cations for dissemination of knowledge among the ma sses in the form of 
brochures, folders and guide books under the informative series. These are being published in English, Hindi and other regional 
languages also. So far no such literature has been brought out in any other foreign language. 

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
26.  The Committee had noted while examining Demands for  Grants (2010-11) that utilization of allocation fo r this 
purpose was very poor and explanation given was not  convincing. Action Taken Reply also does hardly ad d anything 
new. The Committee expresses its concern again abou t the manner in which the awareness generation acti vity is being 
handled.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
27.  Further, there is need for generating interest  amongst general public, specially children, by put ting some special 
programme such as puppet show, documentary etc. Mor eover, the display boards should be made bilingual and it should have 
all the relevant information about a particular sit e. Brochures should be made available in local lang uage also NGOs/College 
students may also be roped in to act as volunteers/guides to ensure. the local participation.  (para 33 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
28.  Under the Cultural Awareness programs, photogr aphic exhibition, painting competition, debates and  similar other 
programs are being organized for school and college  students by the regional offices of the ASI throug hout country on 
special/heritage days/week. Bilingual display board s with relevant information are provided by the loc al offices of ASI. 
Brochures in local languages are also available at ticketed and important monuments. These programs ar e held during the 
special/heritage days/week, these are being celebrated with the participation of school and college students. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
33.  The Committee notes the steps taken by the ASI  in involving school children in their effort to popularize and preserve our 
monuments. The Committee recommends that the local community and the students of local colleges and ed ucational

administrative approval for carrying out constructi on works on purchase of some property from ASI and other competent 
authorities and by when the work would be complete. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
104.  The Committee notes that National Archives of  India has highly competent professionals in the fi eld of Archives record 
management, conservation, reprography and other related field of Archival Science. The National Archives has the great task of 
managing records. The Committee is also of the view  that the National Archives should conduct regular courses for the 
employees of Government offices and if possible dep ute staff from its organization to assist various o ffices to maintain record 
in a better way. However, the Committee notes that the plan outlay of Rs. 4.50 crore made in BE 2009-1 0 was reduced to Rs. 
3.75 crore at RE stage. Again an amount of Rs. 5.00  crore has been provided in BE 2010-11. The Committ ee feels that there is 
some sort of inconsistency in the planning which ha s resulted in the fluctuation of plan outlay at BE and RE stages which can 
affect the functioning and activities of the National Archives of India. 
(para 95 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
105.  The National Archives of India is running a p ost Graduate One Year Diploma Course in Archives an d Records 
Management as well as short term certificate course s in various disciplines of Archives keeping includ ing Records 
Management, Reprography, Care and Conservation of Books, Manuscripts and Archives at professional level and Servicing and 
Repairs of Records at Sub-Professional level which are being attended by the private candidates as wel l as sponsored staff 
members from various State Archives and Central Gov ernment offices. In addition, the Department is run ning a regular 
programme for Departmental Records Officers of the Government Departments to guide them in maintaining  their records in a 
proper and scientific manner. The Department is als o deputing its officers from time to time to inspec t Departmental Records 
Rooms of the Government Departments and advice them  accordingly on various related Record Management i ssues. Besides 
conducting regular courses, the National Archives o f India is also conducting on request training prog rammes in Records 
Management, Digitization/Microfilming and Conservat ion, for the benefit of the Government employees of  public sector 
undertakings and libraries etc. in different parts of the country in collaboration with them. Similarly, programmes are also being 
conducted in collaboration with them. Similarly, pr ogrammes are also being conducted in collaboration with the States/UT 

Archives and State Governments in Human Resource De velopment in the field of Archives, Records Managem ent, 
Conservation and Reprography. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
106.  The Committee noted the reply.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
107.  The Committee notes that India has a number o f Museums under its control, both Government and pr ivate. The 
allocations to the Museums is enough as is evident from the utilization of allocation under Museum head. In 2009-10, allocation 
of Rs. 72.36 crore was made. The actual expenditure  upto 31st March, 2010 is Rs. 71.50 crore. However,  there is need for 
detailed pamphlets listing numerous exhibitions, IMAX and Space Shows, optional audio tours for an extra fee, special lectures 
and the Restaurants which can create interest in the minds of people.  (para 104 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
108.  The museums under the control of Government h ave been persuaded for nearly 1/2 years on a regula r basis to embark 
upon the 14-point reforms agenda, which include the suggestions given by the Parliamentary Standing Committee. An appraisal 
of the progress made is being done constantly, with Museum Heads being called for meetings, specifically on the subject. They 
are also being enthused to adopt 14-points through various BoT and Advisory Group meetings. Museums ha ve been spurred 
into action and most of them have started showing results on the suggested areas. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
109.  The Committee notes the reply.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
110.  There is also need to review the timings of t he Museum which should be extended in evening hours  keeping in view that 
in most part of India, days are very hot. During Sc hool vacations, time should be extended so that chi ldren can visit it in the 
evenings with their parents.   (para 105 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
111.  This has been deliberated upon and museums ha ve been asked to adopt flexible timings as per loca l conditions. The 
National Gallery of Modern Art has formed a separat e Sub-Committee to look into this subject. During t he impending 
Commonwealth Games, both National Museum and National Gallery of Modern Art have extended their hours till 9.00 p.m. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
112.  The Committee recommends that keeping in view  the weather conditions, the Museums should be opened in evening also 
by deputing more staff.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
113.  Further, Security should be strengthened in a ll the museums. The punishment for doing any damage  to the museum 
should be explicity displayed at all the prominent places.  (para 106 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
114.  Security is one key issue on the reforms agen da of the museums. Some of the iconic museums like Indian Museum and 
Vitoria Memorial Hall are in the process of handing  over the security to CISF. National Museum and Sal arjung Museum 
already have CISF cover. NGMA has an elaborate priv ate security apparatus in place. Besides the physic al security, the 
Museums already have appliances like CCTVs etc. in place and already in the process of further augment ing the security 
through modern x-ray machines at entrance, etc. 
 
 

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
115.  The Committee notes the reply and recommends that modern equipments and gadgets need to be used for securing 
the museums and their objects.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
116.  More than that India’s brilliant IT and engin eering brains could be garnered to design new and e xciting exhibits, marking 
the beginning of transforming museums into “edutainment” destinations.  
(para 107 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
117.  It is acknowledged that the role of IT has no t been utilized to the required extent till now. Ho wever, National Council of 
Science Museums is being involved with all the proc esses requiring IT intervention. In various museums , an offer from the 
British Council to educate museum professionals into ways of transforming museums into education sectors is being deliberated 
upon in the Ministry. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
118.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should n ot delay the opportunity from British Council to ed ucate 
museum professional and get the benefit from their expertise.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
119.  The Committee notes that the Central Secretar iat Library with a huge depository of books and volumes are not accessible 
to the common public due to security reasons. The C ommittee recommends that the Central Secretariat Li brary may be moved 
out of the high security area and housed at a place  where the researchers, students, academicians and general public can access 
it. The Ministry of Culture may also explore the possibility of constructing a new campus for the Central Secretariat Library. 
        (para 112  ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
120.  The Central Secretariat Library (CSL) has a c ollection of 6.5 lakhs volumes. It has also two Bra nch Libraries located at 
Bahawalpur House and R.K. Puram. The Tulsi Sadan Li brary located at Bahawalpur House is primarily mean t for books in 
regional languages whereas the R.K. Puram Library caters to the needs of Government employees working in adjoining areas. 
121.  The main Library in Shastri Bhavan has a rese arch collection in the Area Study Division. It has a rich collection of 
Government documents including the Reports and docu ments published before Independence. The use of thi s collection has 
reduced in recent years due to strict security meas ures. The CISF has been advised to allow entry of s tudents, academicians/ 
researchers in Shastri Bhavan. 
122.  The Ministry of Culture is exploring the possibility of shifting CSL to another building possibly in Indira Gandhi National 
Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) located in the Central Vista area. The IGNCA Trust has been requested to provide a suitable space 
for CSL. The matter is under consideration. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
123.  The Committee notes the reply.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
124.  The allocation to the Public Libraries was Rs . 40.62 crore in the year 2009-10. The expenditure upto 31st March, 2010 is 
Rs. 40.13 crore. The Committee is of the view that the Government should provide funds to the Librarie s through Ministry of 
Culture, if it can be utilized by them. However, there need to be some improvement as such the catalogue of the libraries should 
be available on internet. The Computers and softwar es installed in the libraries should be in working conditions all the time so 
that readers are not put to inconvenience. The conc ept of community libraries should be explored and t hey should be promoted 
with wide publicity.    (para 120 ibid ) 

Reply of the Government  
125.  Ministry of Culture has asked the Libraries u nder its control to send their requisition for additional funds so that same can 
be considered in the first Supplementary Budget. Fo r public libraries, Raja Rammohun Roy Library Found ation (RRRLF) is 
providing financial assistance under its ‘Matching’  and ‘Non-Matching’ Schemes to more than 13000 Publ ic Libraries all over 
the country which includes Village and Panchayat Li braries. These libraries also function as places fo r social interactions and 
serve the local communities. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
126.  The Committee may be apprised of the additional fun ds required by the Libraries and sought by the Mini stry of 
Culture in the first Supplementary Budget.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
127.  The Committee at the same time observed that wherever large collections did exist, they were not  fully used because of 
rigid rules, Library users were not trusted and were asked security deposit, which every library users may not afford.  
        (para 121 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
128.  Delhi Public Library (DPL) has more than 50 b ranches all over National Capital Territory of Delh i. It does not take 
security deposit from the borrowing members. The membership registration fee is nominal (Rs.2 only) and membership is given 
against an identity proof. However, in most of the State Central Libraries and District Libraries, boo ks are issued against a 
security deposit (normally cost of the borrowed boo k). This is done primarily to prevent loss of books . Most of these libraries 
offer free reading room services and readers can consult books within the library. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
129.  The Committee is also aware that although DPL has m ore than 50 branches but it caters mainly to the ar eas in 
New Delhi. The Community centres in various areas can be used for mobile DPL vans which can be on rotation basis.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
130.  The Committee is at a loss to note that there  is no mechanism to reflect the expenditure incurre d for North-East in the 
same financial year. Thus the Committee finds the accounting procedure complex and it is not known how much expenditure is 
incurred for North-East Region. Besides this how much the excess expenditure includes the component of North-East Region is 
not clear. The committee, therefore, recommends tha t necessary accounting system should be devised in consultation with 
C&AG and simplified to give a true picture of the expenditure incurred in North-East Region.  (para 126 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
131.  The necessary accounting system for monitorin g of the expenditure incurred under NER Head for va rious Cultural 
Organizations and Central Schemes has already been devised by the % CCA from the current financial year. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
132.  The Committee notes the reply.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
133.  The Committee notes that the Government has n either shown any long-term vision nor any substanti al short-term action 
to arrest the decay that has set in. The Ministry of Culture must move its wheels to generate a vision for the future that includes 
a sensible policy towards their missions. The Commi ttee recommends that the National Culture Policy ma y be brought out at 
the earliest.      (para 134 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  

134.  A National Committee for drafting a National Culture Policy was constituted on 11-11-2006, the t erms of the Committee 
was extended up 30-6-2008. The Committee has met si x times but could not arrive at a consensus. The co mmittee members 
have put forth various views and the same are under consideration.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
135.  The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the National Culture Policy would be formulated at the earliest.

having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this One Hundred a nd Sixty Sixth 
Report on “Action Taken by the Government on the Recommendations/Observations of the Committee contained in its

Report were received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the 3 c0th August, 2010.

(i) Recommendations/observations, which have been a ccepted by the Department: 
 Para Nos. 8, 13, 21, 22, 23, 24, 31, 38, 39, 41, 4 6, 51, 57, 62, 67, 71, 74, 75, 76 and 77  Total : 20

 Nil

 Nil

6.  Noted for compliance.

7.  The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  
 

ANNUAL PLAN FOR 2010-11 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE

Reply of the Government  
12.   NACIL and its subsidiaries, Air India Express  and Alliance Air operate regular domestic and inte rnational air

predominantly deployed on the domestic & short haul  international routes. With respect to the mention that “NACIL

of the new A320 family aircraft capacity has been u sed to replace the routes operated by the old B737- 200 aircraft, 
A300 aircraft and A320 aircraft on lease that have been returned to the lessors. Additionally, about 2 0% of the new 
A320 family aircraft capacity has been deployed to replace the wide body equipment on the feeder servi ces for 

international operations in order to minimize costs  of such feeder services and as replacement capacit y on some of the

2008-09 and by 12% during April-May, 2010 compared to April-May, 2009. In the recent past, following

/circle6 Additional frequencies - between Delhi and Mumbai/C hennai/Kolkata/Bangalore/ Patna/ 
Amritsar/Guwahati; 
/circle6 Ahmedabad-Delhi - equipment upgraded from CRJ to A319.

freedom feeds, the domestic and international sched ule of NACIL now generate feeds from both direction s; etc.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
16.   The Committee also feels that the NACIL shoul d revisit the underutilized bilaterals signed in th e past and try to 
add more services with the new aircrafts. 
(Para 22 ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
17.   At present India has signed/initialed bilater al Air Services Agreement with 108 countries. The c apacity 
entitlement available for the designated airlines o f India is 8 lakhs seats/week (approx). Usually, th e designated 
airline(s) of any country are unable to utilize the  total capacity entitlement available with the resp ective country. The 

airlines utilize the capacity entitlements availabl e on different sectors as per their commercial judg ment, which is also 
guided by other factors, such as traffic demand, viability, flow of traffic on that particular route etc. 
18.   Prior to 2003, Air India (erstwhile Indian Ai rlines also) was the Indian carrier who operated on  the international 
sector. At that time, Air India was not able to uti lize the traffic rights or serve the different inte rnational sectors 
substantially due to fleet constraint and other, prevailing reasons. (The position more or less remains same even now). 
19.   In order to pave way for the maximum utilizat ion of traffic rights by Indian carriers, it was de cided to open way 
for the private scheduled carriers also for operati ons in the international sectors. The prime objecti ve of permitting our 
private scheduled airlines to operate on internatio nal sector is optimal utilization of traffic rights  available with us, 
which otherwise remained unutilized due to various factors. 
20.   At present, in order to ensure the maximum ut ilization of traffic rights, the Government is gran ting the traffic 
rights to private scheduled carriers also after giv ing due consideration to the traffic demand of Air India and on those 
sectors where the demand is high. 
21.   Therefore, the utilization of total traffic r ights available to the designated airlines of India  should not be the 
responsibility of Air India alone and Government ne eds to ensure maximum utilization by Air India as w ell as the 
private scheduled carriers (Apart from Jet Airways,  JetLite and Kingfisher Airlines, Spice Jet has alr eady become 
eligible for international operations and Indigo wi ll become eligible from next year as per the guidel ines). Moreover, 
keeping in view the difficult position being faced by our carriers, when the things were getting more and more difficult 
for our airlines during the last two years due to economic slow down and steep rise of ATF prices, the Government has 
been adopting calibrated approach towards granting further bilateral traffic rights. It is expected th at with future 
expansion of fleet of Air India would be in a posit ion to utilize more traffic rights and will be able  to connect more 
foreign destinations.

REPORT
1. The National Museum which was formally inaugurated in August, 1949 in Delhi has in its
possession over 2 lakhs works of exquisite art, both Indian and foreign origin, covering more than
5000 years of cultural heritage. The Museum houses collections of Pre-historic Archaeology,
Archaeology, Anthropology, Jewellery, Paintings, Decorative Arts, Manuscript, Central Asian
Antiquities, Numismatics, Arms and Armour pre-Columbian and Western Art epigraphy, etc. The
National Museum initially housed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, was shifted to its present building at
Janpath in the year 1960. It is now within the administrative control and fully financed by the
Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
2. National Museum was set up with the following vision:-
(i) To Collect antiquities and art objects of historical, cultural and artistic significance for
their protection, preservation and research;
(ii) To disseminate knowledge about significance of the objects, their history, culture and
artistic excellence;
(iii) To serve as a cultural center for enjoyment and interaction of people in and around
artistic and cultural activity; and
(iv) To serve as the National Art Treasure House
3. The Committee had received some inputs about the prevailing state of affairs in all the
Museums under the Union Ministry of Culture, particularly about the National Museum, New Delhi.
The issue was placed before the Committee and it was decided to go into the affairs of this
Museum. Accordingly, it also decided to make an on-the-spot visit of the Museum, which was done
on the 14
th September, 2010.
4. During the interactions with the Museum authorities and those from the Ministry, the
following major issues came up on which the observations/recommendations of the Committee have
been given in the following paragraphs:
